/* obdd — capture daemon: Mode 01 requests over the Bluetooth OBD2 adapter (D-012, D-019).
 *
 * M3 target: real Mode 01 replies from a real car into the ring.
 *
 * Design intent (see docs/DESIGN.md §1): open /dev/obd, a udev symlink to the RFCOMM
 * tty the kernel binds to the adapter (/dev/rfcomm0); initialise the adapter (ATZ, ATE0, ATSP0); then round-robin the PID list at a fixed
 * request budget, one request outstanding at a time. Every timeout and every unanswered
 * PID is logged — a PID the car stops answering is a fault the analysis must see, not a
 * gap to fill.
 */
#include "common/log.h"

int main(void)
{
    log_init("obdd", LOG_INFO);
    LOG_I("start");

    /* TODO(M2): open /dev/obd (O_RDWR | O_NOCTTY); raw line discipline. The baud is
     *           ignored over RFCOMM, so any cfsetspeed() value works.
     * TODO(M2): treat a hangup (read() == 0, EIO, POLLHUP) as "link down": log it,
     *           mark the adapter absent, and reopen with backoff (DESIGN.md §3). The
     *           Bluetooth link drops; that is not a crash.
     * TODO(M3): adapter init; round-robin Mode 01 requests; parse each reply into a
     *           ring_slot_t and push it into the shm ring with src = live.
     * TODO(M3): per-request timeout; log unanswered PIDs; ATZ reset, then back off.
     * TODO(M4): instrument reply-arrival -> push latency into a histogram. */

    LOG_W("not implemented — M0 scaffold");
    return 0;
}
/* supervisor — mechanism E.
 *
 * A diagnostic recorder that dies silently has actively harmed its user, who believes
 * it is on duty. Any child may be kill -9'd at any time; the system degrades, logs,
 * and recovers.
 *
 * The subtle requirement: a PHYSICALLY UNPLUGGED sensor is not a crash. Restarting a
 * child in a tight loop because its hardware is gone is a restart storm, and it is the
 * failure mode most likely to appear at hour 31 of the soak.
 */
#include "common/log.h"

#include <stdio.h>

int main(void)
{
    log_init("supervisor", LOG_INFO);
    LOG_I("start");

    /* TODO(M3): fork/exec children; fd hygiene across fork; waitpid loop.
     * TODO(M3): restart policy with exponential backoff + a restart-storm guard.
     * TODO(M3): hourly heartbeat per child (log_heartbeat) — the soak plot needs it.
     * TODO(M4): degrade-not-die when a sensor is absent; distinguish absent from
     *           crashed and log the distinction. Demo day will unplug something. */

    LOG_W("not implemented — M0 scaffold");
    return 0;
}
/* analyzed — the intelligence. All of it ours (handout §3.3, D-004).
 *
 * Pipeline:
 *   operating-point bin (RPM x load x coolant temp)
 *     -> per-bin running mean/variance
 *     -> multivariate residual (Mahalanobis)
 *     -> robust trend (Theil-Sen) over each sensor's drift from normal
 *     -> fault-area classifier (our weights, our C inference; D-021)
 *     -> state machine with hysteresis and dwell
 *
 * The restraint rule: a monitor that cries wolf twice gets unplugged, and an unplugged
 * monitor is worse than none. False-positive rate is a first-class metric.
 */
#include "common/log.h"

#include <stdio.h>

int main(void)
{
    log_init("analyzed", LOG_INFO);
    LOG_I("start");

    /* TODO(M3): read committed records from storaged's log as it grows, never the ring
     *           (D-031); never read past the durable offset storaged publishes after
     *           fsync returns.
     * TODO(M3): operating-point binning + running statistics (Welford).
     * TODO(M4): Mahalanobis residual; Theil-Sen trend; state machine.
     * TODO(M4): checkpoint baselines to A/B slots; at start, load the newest valid
     *           slot and redo the committed batches after its offset (D-025).
     * TODO(M4): load weights from models/; inference in C. NO network, ever. */

    LOG_W("not implemented — M0 scaffold");
    return 0;
}
/* obdctl — query CLI over a Unix domain socket.
 *
 * The handout is explicit that a crisp CLI with exact semantics beats a pretty
 * dashboard, and it is far more extensible at the live-modification station on demo
 * day. Resist the web app.
 *
 * This is the ONLY directory in src/ permitted to contain network code, and only for
 * the LAN interface (CLAUDE.md §2.1). `make boundary` enforces that.
 */
#include "common/log.h"

#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>

static int usage(void)
{
    fputs("usage: obdctl <verb>\n"
          "  status                     liveness, per-process RSS, event counts\n"
          "  verdicts [--since WHEN]    current and historical diagnoses\n"
          "  series PID --from --to     raw or binned history\n"
          "  baseline PID               learned model for an operating-point bin\n"
          "  faults                     detection / degradation / recovery events\n",
          stderr);
    return 2;
}

int main(int argc, char **argv)
{
    if (argc < 2) return usage();

    log_init("obdctl", LOG_WARN);

    static const char *verbs[] = { "status", "verdicts", "series", "baseline", "faults" };
    for (size_t i = 0; i < sizeof verbs / sizeof verbs[0]; i++) {
        if (strcmp(argv[1], verbs[i]) == 0) {
            /* TODO(M3): connect to the supervisor's UDS and issue the request. */
            printf("%s: not implemented — M0 scaffold\n", verbs[i]);
            return 0;
        }
    }
    return usage();
}

	@# Source only: no build trees, no Mac venv, no raw drive data or soak logs, no transcripts.
	rsync -a --exclude /build --exclude /.git --exclude /.venv --exclude /data \
	      --exclude /soak/logs --exclude /partners ./ $(PI):~/carwatch/
	ssh $(PI) 'cd ~/carwatch && make'

clean:
	rm -rf $(BUILD)

-include $(shell find $(BUILD) -name '*.d' 2>/dev/null)
# tools/ — Python is allowed here (and in its tests, `tests/tools/`) only

Per the handout: the systems core is C; the interface layer may use anything, but **no
graded mechanism may hide in it.** Nothing in this directory is part of the shipped
product's runtime path.

**Present:**

| Tool | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `board_sync.py` | Mirrors the checklist in `docs/milestones.md` onto GitHub issues and the project board. Not a product tool at all — it is how the plan is maintained. See `docs/BOARD/BOARD.md`. |
| `pidscan.py` | Mode 01 supported-PID survey for one car: protocol, battery, VIN hash, one reading per PID. Feeds `pid-survey.md`, which sets each testbed's inputs (**D-022**). |
| `obdlog.py` | The drive logger: every supported PID to `data/drive-*.jsonl` (**D-033**), rpm and load one request in four (`--fast`), static PIDs once into the header, every answering ECU's line kept (**D-044**). Run book: `docs/hardware/first-drive.md`. |
| `obdsim.py` | The fake OBD2 port: an ELM327 emulator on a pty with a scripted drive (`--two-ecu` makes a second ECU answer some PIDs), for development and tests, never the soak's data source (**D-023**). Sessions against it are labeled `synth`. |
| `obdsum.py` | Per-session and per-PID summary of a drive log: rates, gaps, events. |
| `obdplot.py` | PNG figures of a drive log: every PID on one time axis, speed against rpm, reply intervals. |
| `obdview.py` | One offline HTML page per drive log to scrub, zoom and read every PID at once. |
| `obdbins.py` | Operating-point binning prototype: per rpm x load cell, each PID's mean and spread. A look at the data, not the product's analysis. |
| `obdlib.py`, `elm.py`, `macgps.py` | Shared code: reply parsing and PID decoding; one adapter session; optional Mac location. |

**Planned — not written yet.** Listed so nobody looks for them:

| Tool | Purpose | Board item |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `replay.py` | Feed an `obdlog` capture through the real pipeline at its recorded timing, labeled `replay` (a `synth` capture stays `synth`). A legitimate systems artifact (handout §5). Today it is an M0 stub that exits 1. | `replay`, `replayjsonl` |
| `plot_soak.py` | RSS / CPU / event-count series from soak heartbeats → the figure docs/EVALUATION.md §3 requires. | `plots` |

**Setup:** `make toolcheck` builds `.venv/` from `requirements-analysis.txt` (pyserial,
matplotlib, numpy) and runs the tool tests in `tests/tools/` (D-032). Run a tool as
`PYTHONPATH=tools .venv/bin/python tools/<tool>.py`. Logging alone needs only
`requirements.txt`; `--gps` needs `requirements-gps.txt`.

**The labeling rule is absolute.** Every record and log line these tools produce carries
its `src`: `live` only for `obdlog.py` and `pidscan.py` talking to a real car, otherwise
`replay` or `synth`, all the way through to
the report and the demo screen.

content.text:
This is Camden's session. I've read the board, every Python tool, the C stubs and headers, the Pi scripts and the Forester capture. I haven't changed anything yet.

## Where we stand

- **Built in C:**
  - Storage (`storaged`): append-only and crash-consistent.
  - The shared-memory ring that carries readings from capture to storage.
  - The phone page server (`statusd`), still showing synth data.
- **Still empty C stubs:** `obdd` (the capture daemon), `supervisor`, `analyzed` and `obdctl`.
- **Python only:** everything that actually talks to the car. Its replies are already in the format the ring expects: one value per reply, labeled live, replay or synth.
- **Proven:** the Python path read the Forester at 20.7 samples/s across 40 sensors (`captures/forester/`).
- **`make` is still red on this Mac.** `statusd` uses Linux-only calls (board item `macbuild`, #188). The Pi will be our first real C build target.

## What becomes C and what stays Python

The rubric only requires the **product** to be C. Python in `tools/` is allowed, so most of it should stay.

| Python today | Plan | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `elm.py` (adapter session) | **Port →** `src/obd/elm.c` | Product path: open tty, send command, read to `>`, timeout and resync |
| `obdlib.py` (reply parsing, sensor formulas) | **Port →** `src/obd/pid.c` | Product path. Pure functions; port its tests with it |
| `obdlog.py` main loop | **Port →** `obdd` main | Schedule (rpm and load get one request in four), wait while the bus is asleep, reconnect with backoff, push to ring |
| `obdsim.py` (fake car on a pty) | **Keep** | It becomes our desk car for testing the C code |
| `pidscan.py`, `obdsum.py`, `obdplot.py`, `obdview.py` | **Keep** | Offline survey and analysis tools |
| `obdbins.py` | Keep; its idea becomes C in `analyzed` later (M4) | It's a prototype |
| `replay.py` (a stub) | **Needs a decision** | Python can't easily push into the ring; a C replay mode in `obdd` is simpler |
| `board_sync.py` | Keep | Process tool, not product |

So the real conversion is about 500 lines of Python becoming one C daemon, `obdd`. The supervisor, `obdctl` and analysis were never in Python; they're new C work.

## What we can do at the desk with no car

The key point: **`obdsim.py` creates a pty that looks exactly like `/dev/obd`.** We can write `obdd` in C and test it end to end at the desk, on the Pi: fake car → `obdd` → ring → `storaged` → disk → phone page. The data is labeled synth.

We can also run Python `obdlog` and C `obdd` against the same fake car and compare their output.

**One hardware catch:** the OBDLink LX takes its power from the car's OBD port (12 V on pin 16), so it's dead on a desk. To pair it without driving, either:
- sit in the parked car for five minutes (most cars keep pin 16 powered with the key off), or
- feed it from a 12 V supply through an OBD2 female breakout.

Pairing, `rfcomm bind`, `/dev/obd`, and the reply to `ATZ` with no engine running are all things to capture as evidence for board item `bench` (#18).

## Tonight's plan, in order

1. **Bring the Pi up on your new supply** (~30 min, you):
   - Flash Raspberry Pi OS Lite 64-bit with SSH enabled.
   - Run `vcgencmd get_throttled` once idle and once during a `make -j4`.
   - `0x0` both times is the evidence that the supply is good. Paste it.
2. **Write `scripts/provision_pi.sh` and `install.sh` for real** (me, board item `provision`):
   - Packages, bluez, the dialout group.
   - A systemd unit for `rfcomm bind` and the udev rule for `/dev/obd`.
   - Before relying on `rfcomm`, check `command -v rfcomm` on your Pi. Newer bluez may have dropped it, and I won't guess.
3. **`make deploy PI=pi@<host>`, then `make`, `make test` and `make asan` on the Pi.** This is the first proof the C core builds on the target, and it sidesteps the Mac build problem.
4. **Make Python `obdlog` run on the Pi against `obdsim`.** This is the fastest way to "ready": the Pi can log real baseline data on your next drive while the C `obdd` is still being written (board item `pilogger`, #164).
5. **Start the C `obdd` port** on branch `camden/m3/obdd`. CLAUDE.md requires a plan you approve before any multi-file work. Proposed commits:
   1. Sensor formula table and reply parser, with `test_obdlib.py`'s cases ported to C.
   2. Adapter session, tested against a pty in a C test.
   3. The `obdd` loop pushing into the ring.
   4. An integration test: fake car → `obdd` → `storaged` → log, with no sequence gaps.

## Decisions I need from you or Lance before step 5 lands

- **Label for the fake car:** should `obdd` label data synth when the adapter announces itself as the simulator, as `obdlog` does? I'd say yes.
- **When two engine computers answer one request:** `obdlog` keeps every reply line, but a ring slot holds one. Keep the first and log an event when more than one answers?
- **Sensors read once at start** (13, 1C, 51 on the Forester): store them as a startup event record?
- **VIN hash:** needs SHA-256 written in C. Skip it in `obdd` for now?
- **Replay:** C `obdd --replay FILE`, or keep the Python plan?
- **Dev machine:** fix the Mac build (#188) now, or treat the Pi and Linux CI as where C gets built?

Also, `m2.zip` is sitting untracked in the repo root. It should move out or go in `.gitignore` before any commit.

# Design document — carwatch

Camden Thomas and Lance Baron · CS 370, Colorado State University · M2, 2026-10-28

**User and problem.** Lance drives a 2015 CR-V daily, and nothing reads his engine's
sensors except a check-engine light that speaks only once something has failed. carwatch
is a box that boots at every key-on, records every Mode 01 sensor through a Bluetooth
OBD2 dongle, learns *this* car's normal, and flags behavior that leaves it before the
light would. It is also tested on Camden's 2008 Forester (D-022), which made the first
live capture on 2026-10-28 (`captures/forester/20261028T220659.957/`). **Claim (D-021):**
it learns the normal of the car it is installed in, flags behavior outside it and names
the likely fault area, with measured catch and false-alarm rates on faults we induce.

**Scope.** The product is a Raspberry Pi 4 on the owner's own USB-C charger, an OBDLink
LX dongle read over Bluetooth, and a phone page over the box's own Wi-Fi, with a clock
module and a tri-color light on the Pi's header. It is deliberately that small: the
engine's own sensors, 43 of them on the Forester, are the cooperating sensors, and every
key-off is a power cut that the storage layer is built to survive. Nothing is cut or wired
into the car, and nothing of ours is added to it: no sensor, battery, supercapacitor or
cooling. The TA agreed to this scope on 2026-10-28; §7 prices it.

*`D-###` cites an entry of our decision log, kept in git history
(`git show 8c09b3d:docs/DECISIONS.md`).*

## 1. Architecture

```text
OBD2 port -- OBDLink LX (Bluetooth Classic SPP, D-019); the Forester speaks CAN 11-bit/500 k
   ~~ RFCOMM ~~> BlueZ -> /dev/rfcomm0 -> /dev/obd
  obdd       Mode 01, one request outstanding; 20.7 replies/s measured (Mac, see below),
    |        request cycle p50 42 ms, p99 91 ms; rpm and load 2.6 Hz, each other PID 0.4 Hz
    | ring: SPSC in shared memory, 20.7 slots/s; refuse and count when full, never overwrite
    v
  storaged [D]  BEGIN..records..COMMIT, one fsync per second or 64 samples;
    ^           1.2 KB/s, about 4 MB per running hour -> 16 MB segments, ext4 on the SD card
    |           events from every daemon: one SEQPACKET Unix socket, a few per drive (D-042)
    | committed records only, read back from the log, about 1 s behind (D-031)
    v
  analyzed      bins -> baselines -> residuals -> trends -> area rule -> FSM; a few verdicts per drive
    v
  supervisor [E] fork/exec, hourly heartbeats, restart with backoff --GPIO--> light, 1-4 Hz
    ^  Unix socket /run/carwatch/ctl.sock, on demand (D-043)
  obdctl (CLI)   statusd: GET-only HTTP over a poll() loop; page, JSON, CSV -> phone (D-013, D-045)
power: the owner's USB-C charger -> Pi 4. It dies at key-off, so every key-off is a power cut.
```

Every rate above is from the first Forester capture (54 s, 1113 samples, one ECU
answering, no `NO DATA`, no errors), made by the Python logger (D-033) **on a Mac**, whose
Bluetooth stack is not the Pi's: on the Pi, BlueZ shares one radio with the Wi-Fi access
point (`btcoex`), so 20.7 replies/s is the target `obdd` must reach there, not yet a Pi
measurement. Every daemon is single-threaded; each logs a heartbeat at start, hourly and
at every state change. One reply is one sample, one record and one analysis step. Queries
go to the supervisor, which asks the process holding the answer (D-043); `analyzed` never
reads a ring (D-031). `statusd` reads a *source* behind one function; today that source
is synthetic and every row it serves says `src=synth` (D-045), and the real one is a
client of the control socket.

## 2. Mechanism mapping

D and E are the committed pair (D-017). B and F stay declined: 21 samples a second never
stresses a ring, and there is no sensor of our own to drive by interrupt.

| Item | Component | Justification from the user's requirements | Measured by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| D | `storaged`; checkpoints in `analyzed` | Power vanishes at every key-off and whenever the cable is pulled, yet the record and weeks of learned baselines must survive, and no baseline may learn a sample a cut later erased (D-031): append-only CRC'd records, 1 s commits, A/B checkpoints (D-025, D-035) | 50 cable pulls mid-write; records lost per cut; recovery time |
| E | `supervisor`, `src/ipc/` | A recorder that dies silently harms an owner who thinks it is on duty. Analysis, the least trusted code, must not take capture or storage down; the page server, the only network code, must not either | `kill -9` each child 20×: detection, recovery, fd leaks |

**Two distinct sensors that cooperate (handout §3.1).** The coolant thermistor, the
intake-air thermistor, the ambient-air sensor, the manifold pressure sensor, the mass
air-flow sensor and the oxygen sensors are separate transducers; the ECU only carries
their readings, and the dongle relays them. They cooperate inside one pipeline: every
sample is binned by the rpm, load and coolant temperature current when it arrived, and
every diagnostic in §3 fuses at least two of them, so no reading means anything alone.
They are also polled unequally by our choice, not theirs: rpm and load every request
cycle, since the bin axes must be fresh, the rest in round robin (2.6 Hz against 0.4 Hz).
The TA agreed on 2026-10-28 that this satisfies §3.1 without a sensor of our own. "Both
sensors alive" (M2) is the committed live capture; "through the pipeline" (M3) is the same
sensors as committed records labeled `live`.

## 3. Analysis: how normal is learned and a fault area named

All our code (handout §3.3). Per committed sample, `analyzed` (1) bins by rpm × load ×
coolant temperature, so a cold idle is never compared with a warm cruise; (2) keeps per-bin
running mean and covariance (Welford), in A/B checkpoints; (3) scores the Mahalanobis
distance from the bin's baseline, which fires when a *partnership* breaks; (4) fits
Theil–Sen slopes of residuals across drives; (5) names the area by a rule we write: the
sensor group in the table below that carries most of the residual, with no trained model
(decided 2026-10-28); (6) surfaces verdicts through a hysteresis-and-dwell state machine,
and the phone page shows the trends and statistics behind each one.

The Forester publishes every sensor below (`hardware/pid-survey.md`); the CR-V is not yet
surveyed.

| Fault area (D-021) | Cooperating sensors (PIDs) | Signature | Induced by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Cooling | coolant 05, intake air 0F, ambient 46, load 04, speed 0D | warm-up slope or settled temperature off its bin's normal for the same ambient and load | cardboard over the radiator |
| Air/fuel | fuel trims 06 and 07, MAP 0B, MAF 10, rpm 0C, O2 15 and lambda 24 | long-term trim rising at idle with idle MAP, shrinking with load | a small vacuum line opened |
| Sensor/electrical | the failed PID and its usual partners; module voltage 42; at a cold start, coolant, intake air and ambient | one PID absent or flat while its partners move; after a long soak, one temperature off the other two | a sensor unplugged |
| Unknown | all | residual high, no area matches | — |

No row can be called by one threshold on one value: each compares sensors that normally
move together, inside one bin. Drives are ordered by `boot_id`, a cold soak is recognized
by coolant, intake air and ambient agreeing at key-on, and cross-drive trends wait until
wall time is trusted (§6). The first capture already shows the partnerships: parked and
warm, revved between 640 and 2970 rpm, coolant sat at 96–98 °C with intake air at 40 °C
and ambient at 19 °C, and long-term trim averaged −5 % against a mean manifold pressure of
22 kPa.

## 4. Failure-mode table

Log lines are `<process> <level> <event> key=value` with `src`; the table names the event.

| Component | Failure | Detection | Response | Log event |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| adapter | Bluetooth drops | `read` 0/`EIO`, `POLLHUP` | reopen `/dev/obd` with backoff | `link_lost`, `reconnected` |
| adapter | garbage or timeouts | parse failure; timeout | 3 in a row: `ATZ`, then reopen | `reply_bad`, `adapter_reset` |
| adapter | engine off, key in ACC | `0100` gets `NO DATA` | poll `0100` every few s, record nothing | `ecu_silent` |
| ECU | a sensor unplugged or failed | 5 `NO DATA` in a row; or pinned or flat while its partners move; MIL on (PID 01) | mark absent or suspect, retry each minute. ECUs often substitute a value and light the CEL: not caught before the light | `pid_absent`, `pid_flat`, `mil_on`, `pid_present` |
| `obdd` | hangs with the link up: heartbeat alive, no sample pushed | no sample in 10 s with the ECU answering | the supervisor restarts it | `capture_stalled` |
| any child | crash, `kill -9` | `waitpid` | restart with backoff; others run on | `child_exit`, `child_restart` |
| ring | consumer stalls | sequence gap; late heartbeat | refuse and count; restart `storaged`; red | `ring_full`, `heartbeat_late` |
| storaged | power cut mid-write (every key-off) | bad CRC or no `COMMIT` at boot | truncate the tail and the open batch (D-025) | `recovered` |
| storaged | disk full; `fsync` or write `EIO` | `ENOSPC`, return values | drop the oldest segment if allowed; hold the durable offset; degrade, red | `enospc`, `fsync_failed` |
| analyzed | torn checkpoint | slot CRC | load the other slot, redo the batches since | `checkpoint_bad` |
| `statusd` | a bad or oversized request; the CSV report cannot be built (memory) | the parser's limits; the builder's return value | 4xx, 431 or 503; capture unaffected | `request_refused`, `report_failed` |
| supervisor | dies | systemd `Restart=always` | light freezes steady = "not running" | journal (persistent, on the log partition) |
| clock | wall time untrusted at boot (no clock module, or its backup lost) | time before the build date | run on `mono_ns`; records carry `WALL_UNTRUSTED` | `rtc_invalid` |
| power | cable pulled, crank dip, or charger live at key-off | unclean end at the next boot; `vcgencmd` undervoltage; `0100` silent with power on | crash recovery (D); log; a silent ECU with power on is recorded, not a fault | `recovered`, `undervoltage`, `ecu_silent` |
| OS | power cut corrupts the root filesystem | boot fails | the root filesystem is read-only; only the log partition is written (board `rofs`) | journal, on the log partition |
| radio | Bluetooth and Wi-Fi share one chip | reply p99 in the heartbeat | measure (`btcoex`) | heartbeat |

## 5. Storage and data

- **Format (D-034, `include/store/record.h`):** a 40-byte header (`magic`, `kind`, `seq`,
  `mono_ns`, `wall_ns`, `src`, flags, `boot_id`), a typed body, a CRC32 over both. Kinds:

"""obdlib: ELM327 reply parsing, Mode 01 decoding, support bitmaps, VIN handling."""
import unittest

import obdlib
from obdlib import AdapterError, NoData


class ParseResponse(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_single_line_reply_returns_data_after_the_pid(self):
        data = obdlib.parse_response("41 0C 1A F8 \r\r>", 0x01, 0x0C)
        self.assertEqual(data, bytes([0x1A, 0xF8]))

    def test_spaces_off_reply(self):
        self.assertEqual(obdlib.parse_response("410C1AF8\r\r>", 0x01, 0x0C),
                         bytes([0x1A, 0xF8]))

    def test_searching_banner_is_skipped(self):
        raw = "SEARCHING...\r41 0D 3C \r\r>"
        self.assertEqual(obdlib.parse_response(raw, 0x01, 0x0D), bytes([0x3C]))

    def test_first_matching_ecu_wins(self):
        raw = "41 05 5A \r41 05 5B \r\r>"
        self.assertEqual(obdlib.parse_response(raw, 0x01, 0x05), bytes([0x5A]))

    def test_other_pid_reply_is_not_accepted(self):
        with self.assertRaises(AdapterError):
            obdlib.parse_response("41 0D 3C \r\r>", 0x01, 0x0C)

    def test_bus_init_ok_is_skipped_and_its_error_raises(self):
        raw = "BUS INIT: ...OK\r41 0C 1A F8 \r\r>"
        self.assertEqual(obdlib.parse_response(raw, 0x01, 0x0C), bytes([0x1A, 0xF8]))
        with self.assertRaises(AdapterError) as cm:
            obdlib.parse_response("BUS INIT: ...ERROR\r\r>", 0x01, 0x0C)
        self.assertEqual(str(cm.exception), "BUS INIT: ...ERROR")

    def test_no_data_is_its_own_error(self):
        with self.assertRaises(NoData):
            obdlib.parse_response("NO DATA\r\r>", 0x01, 0x5C)

    def test_adapter_errors_raise(self):
        for text in ("?", "BUFFER FULL", "UNABLE TO CONNECT", "CAN ERROR", "STOPPED",
                     "BUS BUSY", "<DATA ERROR"):
            with self.subTest(text=text), self.assertRaises(AdapterError) as cm:
                obdlib.parse_response(text + "\r\r>", 0x01, 0x0C)
            self.assertNotIsInstance(cm.exception, NoData)

    def test_no_bus_is_its_own_error(self):

  card holds years of two-hour days.
- **Retention (D-041):** every segment is kept until the log filesystem is 80 % full, then

  go to the journal, persistent on the same partition, size-capped.
- **fsync (D-035, `include/store/wal.h`):** commit every second; the 64-sample cap only
  bounds a replay burst, since live data brings 21 a second. A cut loses at most a second
  of signals that move over minutes; longer batches would lose warm-up at each cold-start
  reset; per-record `fsync` is about 20× the `fsync` count, and `expbatch` measures what

  recovery is measured in §8):** at boot `storaged`

## 6. The box: hardware and power

A Pi 4 with a 32 GB A2 microSD card and a clock module, in a small shell with one USB-C
port and one light; the OBDLink LX in the car's OBD2 port; the owner's own USB-C charger
and a short cable.
Nothing on the car is cut. Parts: `hardware/BOM.md`; connections: `hardware/wiring.md`.

Power is the charger's: live when the car runs, dead at key-off. The box therefore boots
unattended at every start and loses power at every stop. There is no stored energy and no
clean shutdown; mechanism D is designed for exactly that, and the root filesystem is
mounted read-only so a cut cannot corrupt the operating system (`rofs`). A clock module on

and `analyzed` keeps learning bins but holds cross-drive trends.

content.content:
`D-042` · Drafted M2, 2026-10-27 · **By:** Claude, in Camden's session
· **Reviewed:** Camden ⬜ / Lance ⬜
· **Answers (if signed):** D-031's open item (§B.8) and board item `verdictpath`

**Decision (draft).** Samples travel by the rings; everything else that must be durable
is an **event**, and events travel by one socket.

- **The socket.** `storaged` listens on a Unix domain socket of type `SOCK_SEQPACKET`,
  `/run/carwatch/events.sock`, created by the supervisor's runtime directory, mode 0600.
  One packet is one event: `code` u16, then up to 200 bytes of `key=value` text. A
  sequenced packet socket keeps message boundaries and order and never splits an event.
- **Who sends.** Every daemon sends its own events: `analyzed` its verdicts (and also
  tells the supervisor, which drives the light), the supervisor its child, power and
  clock events, `obdd` and `ambientd` their link and sensor events. The event names are
  the failure table's log events (`docs/DESIGN.md` §4).
- **What `storaged` does.** It writes each event as an `event` record (D-034) in the next
  batch, so an event is durable at the same commit as the samples around it and is
  ordered with them by `seq`.
- **When `storaged` is down.** A sender keeps up to 64 unsent events in memory and drops
  the oldest beyond that, counting the drops; the count is in its heartbeat. Every event
  is also a log line in the journal at the moment it happens, so the journal is the
  record of last resort and the socket never blocks a sender (`MSG_DONTWAIT`).

**Event codes.** High byte by sender, low byte by event: `0x01` supervisor, `0x02`
`obdd`, `0x03` `ambientd`, `0x04` `analyzed` (verdicts), `0x05` `storaged` itself (for
example `recovered`, `segment_dropped`). The table of codes lives in one header,
`include/common/events.h`, and nowhere else.

**Why.** D-031 left this open, and the report (D-028) and `obdctl verdicts --since` need
verdicts and faults on disk, in order with the samples. One socket keeps `storaged` the
only writer of the log (C.1). A packet socket is the simplest IPC that keeps one event
one message. A sender that blocked on a dead `storaged` would let a storage fault stop
capture or analysis, which B.2 exists to prevent.

**Cost.** One more listener in `storaged` and one more fd per sender. Events that arrive
while `storaged` is down and overflow the 64-event queue are lost from the log (but not
from the journal), and the drop count says how many. The socket is `AF_UNIX`, so the
boundary rule must allow it outside `src/interface/` (`make boundary`).

**Alternative rejected.** Each process writing its own event file: several writers, no
common order with the samples, and one more crash-recovery story per file. Events in the
rings: the slot type is sized for a reply, and the supervisor, which has no ring, could
not send.
