#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Clean Raspberry Pi OS -> a box that logs the car at every key-on.
# This script is graded indirectly: if the TA can't boot it, the TA can't grade it.
#
#   scripts/provision_pi.sh               # packages, dialout, venv, data directory
#   scripts/provision_pi.sh <OBD-MAC>     # also bind the paired dongle to /dev/obd at
#                                         # boot and start the logger at every key-on
#
# Run it on the Pi, as the user who will own the box, from the repository root
# (make deploy puts the tree in ~/carwatch). It uses sudo. Running it again changes
# nothing that is already right.
#
# Pairing is by hand, once, with the dongle powered (12 V on OBD pin 16: a parked car,
# or a bench supply on an OBD2 breakout), because it needs a button press or a PIN:
#   bluetoothctl     then: power on / scan on / pair <MAC> / trust <MAC> / quit
#
# Until obdd replaces it, the key-on logger is tools/obdlog.py (D-033): its records are
# labeled live, and it is not the product (DESIGN.md §7).
set -euo pipefail

MAC=${1:-}
REPO=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
USER_NAME=$(id -un)
DATA=/var/lib/carwatch/drives
UNITS=/etc/systemd/system

die() { echo "provision: $*" >&2; exit 1; }

[ "$(uname -s)" = Linux ] || die "run this on the Pi, not on $(uname -s)"
[ "$(id -u)" -ne 0 ] || die "run as the box's user, not root; it calls sudo itself"
[ -f "$REPO/tools/obdlog.py" ] || die "no tools/obdlog.py under $REPO"
if [ -n "$MAC" ]; then
    [[ $MAC =~ ^([0-9A-Fa-f]{2}:){5}[0-9A-Fa-f]{2}$ ]] ||
        die "'$MAC' is not a Bluetooth address (AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF)"
fi

echo "== packages =="
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y build-essential valgrind git bluez python3-venv

echo "== serial access =="
# The logger and obdd open /dev/obd, which the udev rule below gives to dialout.
if id -nG "$USER_NAME" | tr ' ' '\n' | grep -qx dialout; then
    echo "$USER_NAME is already in dialout"
else
    sudo usermod -aG dialout "$USER_NAME"
    echo "$USER_NAME added to dialout: log out and back in before opening /dev/obd by hand"
fi

echo "== tools venv =="
# Logging needs only pyserial (tools/requirements.txt); make test adds the rest.
[ -x "$REPO/.venv/bin/python" ] || python3 -m venv "$REPO/.venv"
"$REPO/.venv/bin/pip" install -q -r "$REPO/tools/requirements.txt"

echo "== data directory =="
sudo install -d -m 0755 -o "$USER_NAME" -g "$USER_NAME" "$DATA"

if [ -z "$MAC" ]; then
    cat <<EOF

Done, except Bluetooth. With the dongle powered, pair it once:
  bluetoothctl     then: power on / scan on / pair <MAC> / trust <MAC> / quit
then run again with its address:
  scripts/provision_pi.sh <MAC>
EOF
    exit 0
fi

echo "== OBD2 adapter: bind $MAC to /dev/obd at boot (D-019) =="
# Evidence, not a guess (CLAUDE.md 8.4): newer bluez builds may leave rfcomm out.
RFCOMM=$(command -v rfcomm || true)
[ -n "$RFCOMM" ] || die "this Pi's bluez has no rfcomm tool: paste 'dpkg -L bluez | grep -i rfcomm' and 'bluetoothctl --version' into the board item 'bench' before going on"
bluetoothctl info "$MAC" 2>/dev/null | grep -q "Paired: yes" ||
    die "$MAC is not paired: pair and trust it with bluetoothctl first"

# rfcomm bind makes /dev/rfcomm0 at once; the Bluetooth link itself opens only when a
# program opens the device, so the unit succeeds with the dongle asleep or away.
sudo tee "$UNITS/carwatch-rfcomm.service" >/dev/null <<EOF
[Unit]
Description=carwatch: bind the OBD2 dongle $MAC to /dev/rfcomm0
After=bluetooth.service
Requires=bluetooth.service

[Service]
Type=oneshot
RemainAfterExit=yes
ExecStart=$RFCOMM bind 0 $MAC 1
ExecStop=$RFCOMM release 0

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
EOF

# Consumers open /dev/obd, never an rfcomm number (docs/hardware/wiring.md).
sudo tee /etc/udev/rules.d/99-obd.rules >/dev/null <<'EOF'
KERNEL=="rfcomm0", SYMLINK+="obd", MODE="0660", GROUP="dialout"
EOF
sudo udevadm control --reload

echo "== key-on logger (pilogger) =="
sed -e "s|@USER@|$USER_NAME|g" -e "s|@REPO@|$REPO|g" -e "s|@DATA@|$DATA|g" \
    "$REPO/systemd/carwatch-obdlog.service" | sudo tee "$UNITS/carwatch-obdlog.service" >/dev/null

sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now carwatch-rfcomm.service
sudo udevadm trigger --subsystem-match=tty
sudo systemctl enable carwatch-obdlog.service
sudo systemctl restart carwatch-obdlog.service

echo
ls -l /dev/rfcomm0 /dev/obd || die "/dev/obd did not appear: paste 'udevadm info /dev/rfcomm0'"
cat <<EOF

The logger starts at every boot and writes $DATA/drive-*.jsonl.
  status:   systemctl status carwatch-obdlog
  its log:  journalctl -u carwatch-obdlog -f
With the dongle unpowered it keeps retrying the connection; that is expected.
EOF

# (make deploy puts the tree in ~/carwatch). It uses sudo. Running it again changes
# nothing that is already right.
#
# Pairing is by hand, once, with the dongle powered (12 V on OBD pin 16: a parked car,
# or a bench supply on an OBD2 breakout), because it needs a button press or a PIN:
#   bluetoothctl     then: power on / scan on / pair <MAC> / trust <MAC> / quit
#
# Until obdd replaces it, the key-on logger is tools/obdlog.py (D-033): its records are
# labeled live, and it is not the product (DESIGN.md §7).
set -euo pipefail

MAC=${1:-}
REPO=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
USER_NAME=$(id -un)
DATA=/var/lib/carwatch/drives
UNITS=/etc/systemd/system

die() { echo "provision: $*" >&2; exit 1; }

[ "$(uname -s)" = Linux ] || die "run this on the Pi, not on $(uname -s)"
[ "$(id -u)" -ne 0 ] || die "run as the box's user, not root; it calls sudo itself"
[ -f "$REPO/tools/obdlog.py" ] || die "no tools/obdlog.py under $REPO"
if [ -n "$MAC" ]; then
    [[ $MAC =~ ^([0-9A-Fa-f]{2}:){5}[0-9A-Fa-f]{2}$ ]] ||
        die "'$MAC' is not a Bluetooth address (AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF)"
fi

echo "== packages =="
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y build-essential valgrind git bluez python3-venv

echo "== serial access =="
# The logger and obdd open /dev/obd, which the udev rule below gives to dialout.
if id -nG "$USER_NAME" | tr ' ' '\n' | grep -qx dialout; then
    echo "$USER_NAME is already in dialout"
else
    sudo usermod -aG dialout "$USER_NAME"
    echo "$USER_NAME added to dialout: log out and back in before opening /dev/obd by hand"
fi

echo "== tools venv =="
# Logging needs only pyserial (tools/requirements.txt); make test adds the rest.
[ -x "$REPO/.venv/bin/python" ] || python3 -m venv "$REPO/.venv"
"$REPO/.venv/bin/pip" install -q -r "$REPO/tools/requirements.txt"

echo "== data directory =="
sudo install -d -m 0755 -o "$USER_NAME" -g "$USER_NAME" "$DATA"

if [ -z "$MAC" ]; then
    cat <<EOF

Done, except Bluetooth. With the dongle powered, pair it once:
  bluetoothctl     then: power on / scan on / pair <MAC> / trust <MAC> / quit
then run again with its address:
  scripts/provision_pi.sh <MAC>
EOF
    exit 0
fi

echo "== OBD2 adapter: bind $MAC to /dev/obd at boot (D-019) =="
# Evidence, not a guess (CLAUDE.md 8.4): newer bluez builds may leave rfcomm out.
RFCOMM=$(command -v rfcomm || true)
[ -n "$RFCOMM" ] || die "this Pi's bluez has no rfcomm tool: paste 'dpkg -L bluez | grep -i rfcomm' and 'bluetoothctl --version' into the board item 'bench' before going on"
bluetoothctl info "$MAC" 2>/dev/null | grep -q "Paired: yes" ||
    die "$MAC is not paired: pair and trust it with bluetoothctl first"

# rfcomm bind makes /dev/rfcomm0 at once; the Bluetooth link itself opens only when a
# program opens the device, so the unit succeeds with the dongle asleep or away.
sudo tee "$UNITS/carwatch-rfcomm.service" >/dev/null <<EOF
[Unit]
Description=carwatch: bind the OBD2 dongle $MAC to /dev/rfcomm0
After=bluetooth.service
Requires=bluetooth.service

[Service]
Type=oneshot
RemainAfterExit=yes
ExecStart=$RFCOMM bind 0 $MAC 1
ExecStop=$RFCOMM release 0

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
EOF

# Consumers open /dev/obd, never an rfcomm number (docs/hardware/wiring.md).
sudo tee /etc/udev/rules.d/99-obd.rules >/dev/null <<'EOF'
KERNEL=="rfcomm0", SYMLINK+="obd", MODE="0660", GROUP="dialout"
EOF
sudo udevadm control --reload

echo "== key-on logger (pilogger) =="
sed -e "s|@USER@|$USER_NAME|g" -e "s|@REPO@|$REPO|g" -e "s|@DATA@|$DATA|g" \
    "$REPO/systemd/carwatch-obdlog.service" | sudo tee "$UNITS/carwatch-obdlog.service" >/dev/null

sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now carwatch-rfcomm.service
sudo udevadm trigger --subsystem-match=tty
sudo systemctl enable carwatch-obdlog.service
sudo systemctl restart carwatch-obdlog.service

echo
ls -l /dev/rfcomm0 /dev/obd || die "/dev/obd did not appear: paste 'udevadm info /dev/rfcomm0'"
cat <<EOF

The logger starts at every boot and writes $DATA/drive-*.jsonl.
  status:   systemctl status carwatch-obdlog
  its log:  journalctl -u carwatch-obdlog -f
With the dongle unpowered it keeps retrying the connection; that is expected.
EOF

1	# carwatch key-on logger (board item pilogger): tools/obdlog.py on /dev/obd from every

M3 process: provision_pi.sh takes a clean Pi to a key-on logging box

WHAT:   provision_pi.sh installs the packages, joins dialout, builds the
        tools venv and the data directory; given the paired dongle's MAC it
        also binds it to /dev/rfcomm0 at boot, links /dev/obd by udev, and
        installs systemd/carwatch-obdlog.service so obdlog runs at every boot.
WHY:    Camden, 2026-11-08: get the Pi reading the car as soon as possible.
        Until obdd exists, the Python logger is the baseline collector the
        board already allows (pilogger #164, D-033, labeled live). Without a
        MAC it stops before Bluetooth, so it can run tonight at a desk where
        the dongle has no 12 V.
REVIEW: The script refuses, with what to paste, if this bluez has no
        rfcomm tool (CLAUDE.md 8.4) instead of guessing a replacement; I have
        not seen a Bookworm Pi's bluez yet. Restart=always plus obdlog's own
        endless retry means the unit never gives up while the dongle is off.
        Claude's choices: the MAC is optional; data goes to
        /var/lib/carwatch/drives; --fsync-sec 1 to match D-035.
VERIFY: shellcheck clean and cspell clean; in an arm64 Debian 12
        container it refuses root, refuses a malformed MAC, and with no sudo
        stops at the first apt-get. Not yet run on a Pi.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

M3 ipc: ring_depth returns a tail and head read as one consistent pair

WHAT:   ring_depth re-reads the tail after reading the head and retries
        until the tail has not moved (at most 64 tries, then clamps to the
        capacity), instead of reading each once.
WHY:    test_ring failed 40 of 200 runs on main (arm64 Debian 12): a third
        party (supervisor, obdctl status) reading the tail, then losing the
        CPU while the consumer took slots and the producer refilled them,
        saw head - old tail above the capacity. An unchanged tail across the
        head read is a snapshot; the producer never lets head pass tail by
        more than the capacity. The test was right; the code was wrong.
REVIEW: The ordering argument: three acquire loads, tail-head-tail, and
        tail only grows. The clamp is a backstop for a reader starved by a
        consumer that moves on every try; Claude chose 64 tries. With the
        clamp removed the retry alone still gave 0 of 200, so the test still
        tests the retry, not the clamp.
VERIFY: 200 runs of build/bin/test_ring: main 40 failed; this commit 0;
        this commit without the clamp 0. make, make test, make asan pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

git add include/common/sha256.h src/common/sha256.c tests/test_sha256.c && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
M3 common: SHA-256 for the VIN hash, checked against FIPS 180-2

WHAT:   Adds sha256_init/update/final and a one-shot sha256() in
        src/common/sha256.c, with tests/test_sha256.c holding the standard's
        examples: "abc", the empty string, the 448-bit two-block message, and
        a million 'a' fed in 997-byte pieces.
WHY:    Camden, 2026-11-08: obdd hashes the VIN now, not later. The hash
        must equal tools/obdlib.py's vin_hash (first 12 hex of SHA-256) so a
        C session and a Python one of the same car carry the same label
        (D-033). No library: the product links nothing it did not write.
REVIEW: The padding branch in sha256_final when 56 or more bytes are left
        in the block (the 448-bit vector exercises it), and the big-endian
        length bytes.
VERIFY: test_sha256 passes plain and under ASan + UBSan in arm64 Debian 12.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
git add include/obd/pid.h src/obd/pid.c tests/test_pid.c && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
M3 obd: parse ELM327 replies and decode Mode 01 PIDs in C, as obdlib.py does

WHAT:   Adds src/obd/pid.c, the C port of tools/obdlib.py: reply lines,
        obd_parse_all (every answering ECU's line, up to 8), obd_check_bus,
        the Mode 01 decode table, support bitmaps, the Mode 09 VIN and its
        hash; tests/test_pid.c ports every case of test_obdlib.py.
WHY:    obdd needs the logger's reading of the protocol, unchanged: the
        Forester's first capture was decoded by the Python. Python's
        exceptions become a status: NoData, BusAsleep, any other
        AdapterError -> OBD_NODATA, OBD_ASLEEP, OBD_ERROR. Closes #200 with
        the commit before it.
REVIEW: The formulas keep Python's order of operations in double, so values
        are bit-identical. Claude's limits, each documented in pid.h: lines
        over 256 characters are ignored, data past 16 bytes per line is cut,
        VIN frames past index 15 are dropped, a non-ASCII VIN byte becomes '?'
        (Python: U+FFFD), and the 0xE0 block's next-block bit is not wrapped

M3 obd: one ELM327 session over a tty in C, as elm.py runs it

WHAT:   Adds src/obd/elm.c: open the tty raw, send one command, read to the
        `>` prompt under a monotonic deadline with poll(), resync after a
        timeout (wait for the late prompt, then a bare CR), init, the
        supported-PID walk, ATDP, ATRV and the VIN; tests/test_elm.c drives
        it against a scripted adapter on a real pty.
WHY:    obdd's link to the car (#201). It follows tools/elm.py, which ran
        the Forester's first capture: a late reply must never be read as the
        answer to the next request, and a dropped Bluetooth link (read 0,
        EIO, POLLHUP) must be "link lost", which obdd survives (DESIGN.md
        §4), not a crash. A SIM banner is what labels obdsim's data synth
        (Camden, 2026-11-08).
REVIEW: read_to_prompt's order: POLLIN is read before POLLHUP is believed,
        so a reply that lands with the hangup is not lost. One divergence
        from elm.py, Claude's: NUL bytes are skipped when looking for the
        prompt, where Python's rstrip would wait for a timeout.
VERIFY: test_elm passes plain and under ASan + UBSan, 0 failures in 50
        runs. A scratch program (not committed) against tools/obdsim.py
        --two-ecu 05 read the banner (sim=1), the supported list the synth
        fixture's header lists, VIN hash bb984ebda934, and rpm.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

/* Every event code in the product, in one table (D-042): the high byte names the sender,
 * the low byte the event. An event is one `key=value` line of at most 200 bytes, stored by
 * storaged as an event record (D-034) and also written to the sender's journal the moment
 * it happens. The names are DESIGN.md §4's log events.
 *
 * A code, once written to a log, keeps its meaning forever: retire codes, never reuse. */
#ifndef CARWATCH_EVENTS_H
#define CARWATCH_EVENTS_H

#define EV_SENDER_SUPERVISOR 0x01u
#define EV_SENDER_OBDD       0x02u
/*      0x03 was ambientd's, cut on 2026-10-28 with the probe; not reused. */
#define EV_SENDER_ANALYZED   0x04u
#define EV_SENDER_STORAGED   0x05u

#define EV_SENDER(code) ((unsigned)(code) >> 8)

/* obdd (Camden, 2026-11-08: the startup reads and a second ECU are events). */
#define EV_OBD_SESSION      0x0201u   /* adapter= protocol= voltage= vin_hash= supported= */
#define EV_OBD_STATIC_PIDS  0x0202u   /* the PIDs read once at start: 13=03 1C=03 51=01 */
#define EV_OBD_LINK_LOST    0x0203u
#define EV_OBD_RECONNECTED  0x0204u
#define EV_OBD_REPLY_BAD    0x0205u
#define EV_OBD_ADAPTER_RESET 0x0206u
#define EV_OBD_ECU_SILENT   0x0207u   /* the bus asleep: ignition off, key in ACC */
#define EV_OBD_ECU_AWAKE    0x0208u
#define EV_OBD_PID_ABSENT   0x0209u
#define EV_OBD_PID_PRESENT  0x020Au
#define EV_OBD_MIL_ON       0x020Bu
#define EV_OBD_MULTI_ECU    0x020Cu   /* a PID answered by more than one ECU; the first kept */
#define EV_OBD_REPLAY       0x020Du   /* obdd --replay: which capture, at what speed */

/* storaged's own (wal.h names them for the write-ahead log). */
#define EV_STORE_RING_GEN   0x0501u   /* "ns=<0|1> gen=<hex>": which ring instance fed us */
#define EV_STORE_RING_SEQ   0x0502u   /* "ns=<0|1> seq=<hex>": last ring slot in this batch */

#endif

M3 ipc: events travel to storaged as packets on one Unix socket (D-042)

WHAT:   Adds src/ipc/uds.c: a sender that logs each event, queues up to 64,
        and sends them as SOCK_SEQPACKET packets without blocking, and a
        receiver that listens at mode 0600, accepts up to 8 senders and
        reads without blocking; tests/test_uds.c covers order, overflow,
        a receiver restart and refused packets.
WHY:    The event path D-042 drafted and Camden signed on 2026-11-08 by
        choosing to store obdd's events as records (#202). A sender must
        never block on, or die with, storaged (B.2): MSG_DONTWAIT,
        MSG_NOSIGNAL, drop the oldest past 64 and count it, and reconnect
        on the next send. The journal line comes first, as D-042 requires.
REVIEW: One addition to D-042, Claude's: a src byte after the code, so an
        event keeps its live/replay/synth label like every record (2.7);
        a packet without a valid one is refused and counted. Also: the
        reconnect cap of 2 per flush, and that an event already accepted
        by the socket when storaged dies lives only in the journal.
        DGRAM would need no reconnects; I kept D-042's SEQPACKET.
VERIFY: test_uds passes plain and under ASan + UBSan in arm64 Debian 12;
        make boundary passes (socket() only here and in src/interface/).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

Closes #202. ## Why Camden, 2026-11-08: \`obdd\`'s startup reads (adapter, protocol, VIN hash, supported list, static PIDs) and a second ECU's answer are stored as event records. Today only \`storaged\` can write an event: the ring carries samples only. D-042 had drafted this path; Camden's answer is the sign-off it lacked. It also answers \`verdictpath\` (#162) for \`analyzed\` later. That is a decision line, which I leave for a human to tick. **Milestone:** M3 **Mechanism affected (D / E / none):** D (what reaches the log) and E (a sender never blocks on, or dies with, \`storaged\`) ## Review this hardest - \`ev_flush\` in \`src/ipc/uds.c\`: \`MSG_DONTWAIT | MSG_NOSIGNAL\`, and what happens to the head event on \`EPIPE\` (kept, reconnect, at most 2 per flush). - \`take_events\` in \`src/store/main.c\`: an event is read off the socket only when the batch has room for it plus the two ring notes, so none is taken and then dropped. ## What I am least sure about Choices Claude made without a human: - **A \`src\` byte added to D-042's packet** (\`code\`, \`src\`, text), so every event keeps its live/replay/synth label like every record (CLAUDE.md §2.7). A packet without a valid one is refused and counted. - I kept D-042's \`SOCK_SEQPACKET\`. \`SOCK_DGRAM\` on a Unix socket also keeps message boundaries and needs no reconnect after \`storaged\` restarts. So is the content of a batch whose commit fails: \`storaged\` logs \`events_lost count=\`. - \`/run/carwatch/\` must exist (the supervisor's, or systemd's \`RuntimeDirectory=\`). Without it, \`storaged\` logs \`events_disabled\` and records samples anyway. Unrelated, found here: \`tests/tools/test_elm.py\`'s \`test_query_all_returns_every_answering_line\` failed once in this run and passed on the rerun. It reads rpm twice from the simulator's moving drive and expects equal values. content.content:
def connect(path, tries, backoff_min, stop, log=None, idle=None, expired=lambda: False):
    """Open and init the adapter, retrying with exponential backoff. None if stopped,
    out of tries, or past the session's --max-seconds."""
    delay, attempt = backoff_min, 0
    while stop.reason is None and not expired() and (tries <= 0 or attempt < tries):
        attempt += 1
        ad = None
        try:
            ad = elm.Adapter(path)
            ad.init()
            return ad, attempt
        except (elm.LinkLost, obdlib.AdapterError) as e:
            if ad:
                ad.close()
            if log:
                log("connect_failed", attempt=attempt, detail=str(e))
            print(f"obdlog: connect attempt {attempt} failed: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
            if tries > 0 and attempt >= tries:
                break
            end = time.monotonic() + delay
            while stop.reason is None and not expired() and time.monotonic() < end:
                time.sleep(0.05)
                if idle:
                    idle()
            delay = min(delay * 2, 30.0)
    return None, attempt


class Schedule:
    """Which PID to ask next. The --fast PIDs (rpm and load, the binning axes) get one
    request in every FAST_EVERY, taken in turn; every other PID shares the rest,
    round-robin. A PID the caller says to skip (set aside as absent) costs no turn."""

    def __init__(self, pids, fast, every=FAST_EVERY):
        self.fast = [p for p in fast if p in pids]
        self.slow = [p for p in pids if p not in self.fast]
        self.every = every
        self.cursor = {"fast": 0, "slow": 0}
        self.since_fast = 0

    def _take(self, kind, skip):
        group = getattr(self, kind)
        for _ in range(len(group)):
            pid = group[self.cursor[kind] % len(group)]
            self.cursor[kind] += 1
            if not skip(pid):
                return pid
        return None

    def next(self, skip=lambda pid: False):
        """The next PID to request, or None when every PID is skipped."""
        if self.fast and self.since_fast >= self.every - 1:
            pid = self._take("fast", skip)
            if pid is not None:
                self.since_fast = 0
                return pid
        pid = self._take("slow", skip)
        if pid is not None:
            self.since_fast += 1
            return pid
        pid = self._take("fast", skip)
        if pid is not None:
            self.since_fast = 0
        return pid


def read_once(ad, pid):
    """A static PID's answer for the header: every line's hex, or the error text."""
    try:
        return {"raw_all": [a.hex(" ").upper() for a in ad.query_all(1, pid)]}
    except elm.LinkLost:
        raise
    except obdlib.AdapterError as e:
        return {"error": str(e) or type(e).__name__}


def parse_pids(text):
    """'0C,0d, 05' -> [0x0C, 0x0D, 0x05]. ValueError for a bad or empty list."""
    pids = []
    for part in text.split(","):
        part = part.strip()
        try:
            pid = int(part, 16)
        except ValueError:
            raise ValueError(f"{part!r} is not a hex PID") from None
        if not 0 <= pid <= 0xFF:
            raise ValueError(f"{part!r} is not a Mode 01 PID (00 to FF)")
        pids.append(pid)
    return pids


def _run(args, stop):
    t_start = time.monotonic()
    deadline = t_start + args.max_seconds if args.max_seconds else None

    def expired():
        return deadline is not None and time.monotonic() >= deadline

    ad, _ = connect(args.port, args.connect_tries or 0, args.backoff_min, stop)
    if ad is None:
        print(f"obdlog: could not connect to {args.port}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    src = "synth" if (ad.is_sim or args.sim) else "live"
    try:
        supported = ad.supported_pids()
        vin = None
        try:
            vin = ad.vin()
        except obdlib.AdapterError:
            pass
        header = {"tool": TOOL, "schema": SCHEMA, "port": args.port,
                  "adapter": ad.banner, "protocol": ad.protocol(), "voltage": ad.voltage(),
                  "vin_hash": obdlib.vin_hash(vin) if vin else None,
                  "supported": [f"{p:02X}" for p in sorted(supported)]}
        wanted = args.pids if args.pids is not None else sorted(supported)
        static = [p for p in wanted if p in STATIC]
        header["static"] = {f"{p:02X}": read_once(ad, p) for p in static}
    except (elm.LinkLost, obdlib.AdapterError) as e:
        ad.close()
        print(f"obdlog: session setup failed: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    pids = [p for p in wanted if p not in static]
    if not pids:
        # Nothing to poll: the loop would idle until --max-seconds, logging nothing.
        ad.close()
        print("obdlog: no PID left to poll; nothing to log", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    sched = Schedule(pids, args.fast)
    header["pids"] = [f"{p:02X}" for p in pids]
    header["schedule"] = {"fast": [f"{p:02X}" for p in sched.fast],
                          "fast_every": FAST_EVERY if sched.fast else None,
                          "static": [f"{p:02X}" for p in static]}

    out = open_session(args.out, src, args.fsync_lines, args.fsync_sec)
    path = out.path
    out.write("header", **header)

    counts = {"samples": 0, "events": 0, "gps": 0}
    last_event = ["none"]

    def event(name, **fields):
        counts["events"] += 1
        last_event[0] = name + (f" {fields['pid']}" if "pid" in fields else "")
        out.write("event", event=name, **fields)

    gps = None
    if args.gps:
        import macgps  # noqa: PLC0415 - optional
        try:
            gps = macgps.start()
        except macgps.GpsUnavailable as e:
            event("gps_unavailable", detail=str(e))

    no_data = {p: 0 for p in pids}
    absent = {}                       # pid -> monotonic time it was set aside
    multi = set()                     # PIDs already reported as answered by several ECUs
    errors = 0
    asleep_delay = None               # seconds until the next try while the bus is asleep
    next_status = time.monotonic() + args.status_sec
    next_gps = 0.0
    failure = None                    # what ended the session, if it was an exception
    print(f"obdlog: logging {len(pids)} PIDs to {path} (src={src}); Ctrl-C to stop",
          file=sys.stderr)

    def reopen(old_ad):
        """Close the port and reconnect with backoff. None if stopped first."""
        old_ad.close()
        new_ad, attempts = connect(args.port, 0, args.backoff_min, stop,
                                   log=lambda n, **f: event(n, **f), idle=out.tick,
                                   expired=expired)
        if new_ad is not None:
            event("reconnected", attempts=attempts)
        return new_ad

    def poll_gps():
        """Log new location fixes, at most every GPS_POLL_SEC."""
        nonlocal next_gps
        if gps is None or time.monotonic() < next_gps:
            return
        next_gps = time.monotonic() + GPS_POLL_SEC
        fixes, err = gps.poll()
        for fix in fixes:
            out.write("gps", **fix)
            counts["gps"] += 1
        if err:
            event("gps_error", detail=err)

    def wait(seconds):
        """Sleep without missing Ctrl-C, --max-seconds, the fsync bound, the status or the
        location."""
        end = time.monotonic() + seconds
        while stop.reason is None and not expired() and time.monotonic() < end:
            time.sleep(0.05)
            out.tick()
            poll_gps()
            status()

    def status():
        nonlocal next_status
        if time.monotonic() < next_status:
            return
        el = time.monotonic() - t_start
        print(f"[{int(el) // 60:02d}:{int(el) % 60:02d}] "
              f"{counts['samples']} samples, "
              f"{counts['samples'] / el:.1f}/s, {counts['events']} events "
              f"(last: {last_event[0]}), gps {counts['gps']}",
              file=sys.stderr)
        next_status += args.status_sec

    try:
        while stop.reason is None and not expired():
            now = time.monotonic()
            pid = sched.next(lambda p: p in absent and now - absent[p] < ABSENT_RETRY_SEC)
            if pid is None:
                # Every PID is set aside (engine off, ECU quiet): wait for the next retry
                # instead of spinning through an empty pass. The location is still logged.
                time.sleep(0.2)
                out.tick()
                poll_gps()
                status()
                continue
            key = f"{pid:02X}"
            if pid in absent:
                absent[pid] = now          # this is its retry; the next one is a minute on
            try:
                answers = ad.query_all(1, pid)
            except obdlib.NoData:
                no_data[pid] += 1
                event("no_data", pid=key)
                if no_data[pid] == NO_DATA_LIMIT and pid not in absent:
                    absent[pid] = now
                    event("pid_absent", pid=key, after=NO_DATA_LIMIT)
                continue
            except obdlib.BusAsleep as e:
                # Ignition off or ECUs asleep: the adapter is fine, so no reset. Say so
                # once, then try again less and less often until the bus answers.
                errors = 0
                if asleep_delay is None:
                    event("bus_asleep", pid=key, detail=str(e))
                    asleep_delay = args.backoff_min
                wait(asleep_delay)
                asleep_delay = min(asleep_delay * 2, BUS_RETRY_MAX)
                continue
            except elm.LinkLost as e:
                event("link_lost", detail=str(e))
                ad = reopen(ad)
                errors = 0
                if ad is None:
                    break
                continue
            except obdlib.AdapterError as e:
                errors += 1
                event("timeout" if isinstance(e, elm.Timeout) else "adapter_error",
                      pid=key, detail=str(e))
                if errors < ERROR_LIMIT:
                    continue
                errors = 0
                try:
                    event("reinit", banner=ad.init())
                    continue
                except (elm.LinkLost, obdlib.AdapterError) as e2:
                    event("reinit_failed", detail=str(e2))
                # Connected but deaf: close the port and open it again, as for a drop.
                event("reopen", detail="adapter stopped answering")
                ad = reopen(ad)
                if ad is None:
                    break
                continue
            errors = 0
            if asleep_delay is not None:
                asleep_delay = None
                event("bus_awake", pid=key)
            no_data[pid] = 0
            if pid in absent:
                del absent[pid]
                event("pid_present", pid=key)
            # With headers off (ATH0) a line does not say which ECU sent it. Decode the
            # first, as before, and keep every line so the ECUs can be told apart later
            # (D-044).
            raws = [a.hex(" ").upper() for a in answers]
            extra = {"raw_all": raws} if len(raws) > 1 else {}
            if len(raws) > 1 and pid not in multi:
                multi.add(pid)
                event("multi_ecu", pid=key, n_ecu=len(raws), raw_all=raws)
            value, unit = obdlib.decode(pid, answers[0])
            out.write("sample", pid=key, raw=raws[0], val=value, unit=unit,
                      n_ecu=len(raws), **extra)
            counts["samples"] += 1

            poll_gps()
            status()
    except BaseException as e:
        failure = f"error: {type(e).__name__}: {e}"
        raise
    finally:
        reason = (stop.reason or failure
                  or ("max_seconds" if expired() else "link_gave_up"))
        out.write("footer", reason=reason, seconds=round(time.monotonic() - t_start, 3),
                  **counts)
        out.close()
        if ad is not None:
            ad.close()
        if gps is not None:
            gps.stop()
    print(f"obdlog: {counts['samples']} samples, {counts['events']} events -> {path}",
          file=sys.stderr)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    try:
        sys.exit(main())
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        print("obdlog: stopped at once (second interrupt)", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(130)

            delay = min(delay * 2, 30.0)
    return None, attempt


class Schedule:
    """Which PID to ask next. The --fast PIDs (rpm and load, the binning axes) get one
    request in every FAST_EVERY, taken in turn; every other PID shares the rest,
    round-robin. A PID the caller says to skip (set aside as absent) costs no turn."""

    def __init__(self, pids, fast, every=FAST_EVERY):
        self.fast = [p for p in fast if p in pids]
        self.slow = [p for p in pids if p not in self.fast]
        self.every = every
        self.cursor = {"fast": 0, "slow": 0}
        self.since_fast = 0

    def _take(self, kind, skip):
        group = getattr(self, kind)
        for _ in range(len(group)):
            pid = group[self.cursor[kind] % len(group)]
            self.cursor[kind] += 1
            if not skip(pid):
                return pid
        return None

    def next(self, skip=lambda pid: False):
        """The next PID to request, or None when every PID is skipped."""
        if self.fast and self.since_fast >= self.every - 1:
            pid = self._take("fast", skip)
            if pid is not None:
                self.since_fast = 0
                return pid
        pid = self._take("slow", skip)
        if pid is not None:
            self.since_fast += 1
            return pid
        pid = self._take("fast", skip)
        if pid is not None:
            self.since_fast = 0
        return pid


def read_once(ad, pid):
    """A static PID's answer for the header: every line's hex, or the error text."""
    try:
        return {"raw_all": [a.hex(" ").upper() for a in ad.query_all(1, pid)]}
    except elm.LinkLost:
        raise
    except obdlib.AdapterError as e:
        return {"error": str(e) or type(e).__name__}


def parse_pids(text):
    """'0C,0d, 05' -> [0x0C, 0x0D, 0x05]. ValueError for a bad or empty list."""
    pids = []
    for part in text.split(","):
        part = part.strip()
        try:
            pid = int(part, 16)
        except ValueError:
            raise ValueError(f"{part!r} is not a hex PID") from None
        if not 0 <= pid <= 0xFF:
            raise ValueError(f"{part!r} is not a Mode 01 PID (00 to FF)")
        pids.append(pid)
    return pids


def _run(args, stop):
    t_start = time.monotonic()
    deadline = t_start + args.max_seconds if args.max_seconds else None

    def expired():
        return deadline is not None and time.monotonic() >= deadline

    ad, _ = connect(args.port, args.connect_tries or 0, args.backoff_min, stop)
    if ad is None:
        print(f"obdlog: could not connect to {args.port}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    src = "synth" if (ad.is_sim or args.sim) else "live"
    try:
        supported = ad.supported_pids()
        vin = None
        try:
            vin = ad.vin()
        except obdlib.AdapterError:
            pass
        header = {"tool": TOOL, "schema": SCHEMA, "port": args.port,
                  "adapter": ad.banner, "protocol": ad.protocol(), "voltage": ad.voltage(),
                  "vin_hash": obdlib.vin_hash(vin) if vin else None,
                  "supported": [f"{p:02X}" for p in sorted(supported)]}
        wanted = args.pids if args.pids is not None else sorted(supported)
        static = [p for p in wanted if p in STATIC]
        header["static"] = {f"{p:02X}": read_once(ad, p) for p in static}
    except (elm.LinkLost, obdlib.AdapterError) as e:
        ad.close()
        print(f"obdlog: session setup failed: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    pids = [p for p in wanted if p not in static]
    if not pids:
        # Nothing to poll: the loop would idle until --max-seconds, logging nothing.
        ad.close()
        print("obdlog: no PID left to poll; nothing to log", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    sched = Schedule(pids, args.fast)
    header["pids"] = [f"{p:02X}" for p in pids]
    header["schedule"] = {"fast": [f"{p:02X}" for p in sched.fast],
                          "fast_every": FAST_EVERY if sched.fast else None,
                          "static": [f"{p:02X}" for p in static]}

    out = open_session(args.out, src, args.fsync_lines, args.fsync_sec)
    path = out.path
    out.write("header", **header)

    counts = {"samples": 0, "events": 0, "gps": 0}
    last_event = ["none"]

    def event(name, **fields):
        counts["events"] += 1
        last_event[0] = name + (f" {fields['pid']}" if "pid" in fields else "")
        out.write("event", event=name, **fields)

    gps = None
    if args.gps:
        import macgps  # noqa: PLC0415 - optional
        try:
            gps = macgps.start()
        except macgps.GpsUnavailable as e:
            event("gps_unavailable", detail=str(e))

    no_data = {p: 0 for p in pids}
    absent = {}                       # pid -> monotonic time it was set aside
    multi = set()                     # PIDs already reported as answered by several ECUs
    errors = 0
    asleep_delay = None               # seconds until the next try while the bus is asleep
    next_status = time.monotonic() + args.status_sec
    next_gps = 0.0
    failure = None                    # what ended the session, if it was an exception
    print(f"obdlog: logging {len(pids)} PIDs to {path} (src={src}); Ctrl-C to stop",
          file=sys.stderr)

    def reopen(old_ad):
        """Close the port and reconnect with backoff. None if stopped first."""
        old_ad.close()
        new_ad, attempts = connect(args.port, 0, args.backoff_min, stop,
                                   log=lambda n, **f: event(n, **f), idle=out.tick,
                                   expired=expired)
        if new_ad is not None:
            event("reconnected", attempts=attempts)
        return new_ad

    def poll_gps():
        """Log new location fixes, at most every GPS_POLL_SEC."""
        nonlocal next_gps
        if gps is None or time.monotonic() < next_gps:
            return
        next_gps = time.monotonic() + GPS_POLL_SEC
        fixes, err = gps.poll()
        for fix in fixes:
            out.write("gps", **fix)
            counts["gps"] += 1
        if err:
            event("gps_error", detail=err)

    def wait(seconds):
        """Sleep without missing Ctrl-C, --max-seconds, the fsync bound, the status or the
        location."""
        end = time.monotonic() + seconds
        while stop.reason is None and not expired() and time.monotonic() < end:
            time.sleep(0.05)
            out.tick()
            poll_gps()
            status()

    def status():
        nonlocal next_status
        if time.monotonic() < next_status:
            return
        el = time.monotonic() - t_start
        print(f"[{int(el) // 60:02d}:{int(el) % 60:02d}] "
              f"{counts['samples']} samples, "
              f"{counts['samples'] / el:.1f}/s, {counts['events']} events "
              f"(last: {last_event[0]}), gps {counts['gps']}",
              file=sys.stderr)
        next_status += args.status_sec

    try:
        while stop.reason is None and not expired():
            now = time.monotonic()
            pid = sched.next(lambda p: p in absent and now - absent[p] < ABSENT_RETRY_SEC)
            if pid is None:
                # Every PID is set aside (engine off, ECU quiet): wait for the next retry
                # instead of spinning through an empty pass. The location is still logged.
                time.sleep(0.2)
                out.tick()
                poll_gps()
                status()
                continue
            key = f"{pid:02X}"
            if pid in absent:
                absent[pid] = now          # this is its retry; the next one is a minute on
            try:
                answers = ad.query_all(1, pid)
            except obdlib.NoData:
                no_data[pid] += 1
                event("no_data", pid=key)
                if no_data[pid] == NO_DATA_LIMIT and pid not in absent:
                    absent[pid] = now
                    event("pid_absent", pid=key, after=NO_DATA_LIMIT)
                continue
            except obdlib.BusAsleep as e:
                # Ignition off or ECUs asleep: the adapter is fine, so no reset. Say so
                # once, then try again less and less often until the bus answers.
                errors = 0
                if asleep_delay is None:
                    event("bus_asleep", pid=key, detail=str(e))
                    asleep_delay = args.backoff_min
                wait(asleep_delay)
                asleep_delay = min(asleep_delay * 2, BUS_RETRY_MAX)
                continue
            except elm.LinkLost as e:
                event("link_lost", detail=str(e))
                ad = reopen(ad)
                errors = 0
                if ad is None:
                    break
                continue
            except obdlib.AdapterError as e:
                errors += 1
                event("timeout" if isinstance(e, elm.Timeout) else "adapter_error",
                      pid=key, detail=str(e))
                if errors < ERROR_LIMIT:
                    continue
                errors = 0
                try:
                    event("reinit", banner=ad.init())
                    continue
                except (elm.LinkLost, obdlib.AdapterError) as e2:
                    event("reinit_failed", detail=str(e2))
                # Connected but deaf: close the port and open it again, as for a drop.
                event("reopen", detail="adapter stopped answering")
                ad = reopen(ad)
                if ad is None:
                    break
                continue
            errors = 0
            if asleep_delay is not None:
                asleep_delay = None
                event("bus_awake", pid=key)
            no_data[pid] = 0
            if pid in absent:
                del absent[pid]
                event("pid_present", pid=key)
            # With headers off (ATH0) a line does not say which ECU sent it. Decode the
            # first, as before, and keep every line so the ECUs can be told apart later
            # (D-044).
            raws = [a.hex(" ").upper() for a in answers]
            extra = {"raw_all": raws} if len(raws) > 1 else {}
            if len(raws) > 1 and pid not in multi:
                multi.add(pid)
                event("multi_ecu", pid=key, n_ecu=len(raws), raw_all=raws)
            value, unit = obdlib.decode(pid, answers[0])
            out.write("sample", pid=key, raw=raws[0], val=value, unit=unit,
                      n_ecu=len(raws), **extra)
            counts["samples"] += 1

            poll_gps()
            status()
    except BaseException as e:
        failure = f"error: {type(e).__name__}: {e}"
        raise
    finally:
        reason = (stop.reason or failure
                  or ("max_seconds" if expired() else "link_gave_up"))
        out.write("footer", reason=reason, seconds=round(time.monotonic() - t_start, 3),
                  **counts)
        out.close()
        if ad is not None:
            ad.close()
        if gps is not None:
            gps.stop()
    print(f"obdlog: {counts['samples']} samples, {counts['events']} events -> {path}",
          file=sys.stderr)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    try:
        sys.exit(main())
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        print("obdlog: stopped at once (second interrupt)", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(130)

/* Every event code in the product, in one table (D-042): the high byte names the sender,
 * the low byte the event. An event is one `key=value` line of at most 200 bytes, stored by
 * storaged as an event record (D-034) and also written to the sender's journal the moment
 * it happens. The names are DESIGN.md §4's log events.
 *
 * A code, once written to a log, keeps its meaning forever: retire codes, never reuse. */
#ifndef CARWATCH_EVENTS_H
#define CARWATCH_EVENTS_H

#define EV_SENDER_SUPERVISOR 0x01u
#define EV_SENDER_OBDD       0x02u
/*      0x03 was ambientd's, cut on 2026-10-28 with the probe; not reused. */
#define EV_SENDER_ANALYZED   0x04u
#define EV_SENDER_STORAGED   0x05u

#define EV_SENDER(code) ((unsigned)(code) >> 8)

/* obdd (Camden, 2026-11-08: the startup reads and a second ECU are events). */
#define EV_OBD_SESSION      0x0201u   /* adapter= protocol= voltage= vin_hash= supported= */
#define EV_OBD_STATIC_PIDS  0x0202u   /* the PIDs read once at start: 13=03 1C=03 51=01 */
#define EV_OBD_LINK_LOST    0x0203u
#define EV_OBD_RECONNECTED  0x0204u
#define EV_OBD_REPLY_BAD    0x0205u
#define EV_OBD_ADAPTER_RESET 0x0206u

"""obdd end to end at a desk: tools/obdsim.py -> obdd -> ring -> storaged -> the log.

The C daemons as processes, against the fake OBD2 port, with no car. Every sample obdd
pushes must be in the log, labeled synth; the session, supported and static_pids events
must be there too, and a second ECU must be reported once (Camden, 2026-11-08).

Runs where make has built build/bin/obdd and build/bin/storaged (make test builds them
first); skips elsewhere, saying why. It uses the real ring name, so it must not run on a
box whose obdd is live.
"""
import os
import re
import signal
import struct
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time
import unittest
import zlib

import obdsim

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))
BIN = os.path.join(ROOT, "build", "bin")
RING = "/dev/shm/carwatch-obd"           # RING_NAME_OBD (include/ipc/ring.h)

# include/store/record.h: magic, kind, body_len, seq, mono_ns, wall_ns, src, flags,
# reserved, boot_id; then the body; then a CRC32 of both.
HDR = struct.Struct("<IHHQQQBBHI")
REC_MAGIC, REC_SAMPLE, REC_EVENT = 0x31525743, 1, 6
SRC_SYNTH = 3

EV_SESSION, EV_STATIC, EV_MULTI, EV_SUPPORTED = 0x0201, 0x0202, 0x020C, 0x020E
RUN_SECONDS = 8


def records(path):
    """(kind, src, body) for every record in a segment, checking each CRC."""
    data = open(path, "rb").read()
    off = 0
    while off + HDR.size <= len(data):
        magic, kind, body_len, _seq, _mono, _wall, src, _fl, _res, _boot = \
            HDR.unpack_from(data, off)
        if magic != REC_MAGIC:
            raise AssertionError(f"bad magic at {off}")
        end = off + HDR.size + body_len
        (crc,) = struct.unpack_from("<I", data, end)
        if zlib.crc32(data[off:end]) != crc:
            raise AssertionError(f"bad CRC at {off}")
        yield kind, src, data[off + HDR.size:end]
        off = end + 4


@unittest.skipUnless(sys.platform.startswith("linux"), "the ring is POSIX shm on Linux")
@unittest.skipUnless(os.path.exists(os.path.join(BIN, "obdd")) and
                     os.path.exists(os.path.join(BIN, "storaged")),
                     "build/bin/obdd and storaged not built: run make first")
class ObddAgainstSim(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.dir = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        d = self.dir.name
        self.link = os.path.join(d, "obd")
        self.sock = os.path.join(d, "ev.sock")
        self.logdir = os.path.join(d, "log")
        self.sim = obdsim.PtyServer(link=self.link, latency=0.04,
                                    two_ecu={0x05}).__enter__()
        self.procs = []

    def tearDown(self):
        for p in self.procs:
            if p.poll() is None:
                p.kill()
                p.wait()
        self.sim.__exit__(None, None, None)
        if os.path.exists(RING):
            os.unlink(RING)
        self.dir.cleanup()

    def start(self, name, *args):
        out = open(os.path.join(self.dir.name, name + ".out"), "w")
        p = subprocess.Popen([os.path.join(BIN, name), *args], stdout=out,
                             stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
        self.procs.append(p)
        return p

    def stop(self, p):
        p.send_signal(signal.SIGTERM)
        return p.wait(timeout=20)

    def output(self, name):
        return open(os.path.join(self.dir.name, name + ".out")).read()

    def test_every_pushed_sample_and_the_startup_events_reach_the_log(self):
        obdd = self.start("obdd", "--port", self.link, "--create-ring",
                          "--events", self.sock)
        for _ in range(100):                      # obdd makes the ring (bench mode)
            if os.path.exists(RING):
                break
            time.sleep(0.05)
        self.assertTrue(os.path.exists(RING), "obdd created the ring")
        # storaged starts after obdd, so obdd's first events wait in its queue.
        storaged = self.start("storaged", "--dir", self.logdir, "--src", "synth",
                              "--events", self.sock)
        time.sleep(RUN_SECONDS)

        self.assertEqual(self.stop(obdd), 0, "obdd stops cleanly on SIGTERM")
        time.sleep(1.5)                           # one batch: storaged drains the rest
        self.assertEqual(self.stop(storaged), 0, "storaged stops cleanly")

        m = re.search(r"stop samples=(\d+) ring_full=(\d+) events_sent=(\d+) "
                      r"events_dropped=(\d+)", self.output("obdd"))
        self.assertIsNotNone(m, "obdd logged its stop line")
        pushed, ring_full, _sent, dropped = map(int, m.groups())
        self.assertEqual((ring_full, dropped), (0, 0), "nothing refused, nothing dropped")

        recs = []
        for name in sorted(os.listdir(self.logdir)):
            if name.endswith(".cwr"):
                recs += list(records(os.path.join(self.logdir, name)))
        samples = [(src, body) for kind, src, body in recs if kind == REC_SAMPLE]
        events = {}
        for kind, src, body in recs:
            if kind == REC_EVENT:
                code, n = struct.unpack_from("<HH", body)
                events.setdefault(code, []).append((src, body[4:4 + n].decode("ascii")))

        rate = pushed / RUN_SECONDS
        print(f"\n  obdd pushed {pushed} samples in {RUN_SECONDS} s ({rate:.1f}/s), "
              f"log holds {len(samples)}", file=sys.stderr)
        self.assertEqual(len(samples), pushed, "every pushed sample is in the log once")
        self.assertGreater(rate, 10.0, "obdsim answers about 20 a second")
        self.assertTrue(all(src == SRC_SYNTH for src, _ in samples),
                        "obdsim's banner says SIM: every sample is synth")

        coolant = [struct.unpack_from("<BBB5sf", b) for _, b in samples if b[1] == 0x05]
        self.assertTrue(coolant, "coolant was polled")
        self.assertTrue(all(-40.0 <= c[4] <= 215.0 for c in coolant), "coolant decoded")

        for code, what in ((EV_SESSION, "session"), (EV_SUPPORTED, "supported"),
                           (EV_STATIC, "static_pids"), (EV_MULTI, "multi_ecu")):
            self.assertIn(code, events, f"a {what} event is in the log")
        self.assertTrue(all(src == SRC_SYNTH for evs in events.values() for src, _ in evs),
                        "events keep obdd's label")
        session = events[EV_SESSION][0][1]
        self.assertIn("vin_hash=bb984ebda934", session, "the same hash as obdlib.py")
        self.assertIn("carwatch SIM", session)
        self.assertEqual(events[EV_STATIC][0][1], "none", "obdsim has no static PIDs")
        self.assertIn("n=17", events[EV_SUPPORTED][0][1])
        multi = events[EV_MULTI]
        self.assertEqual(len(multi), 1, "a second ECU is reported once per connection")
        self.assertIn("pid=05 n_ecu=2", multi[0][1])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

toolUseResult.originalFile:
# carwatch — CS370 term project
# Systems core is C17 and must stay -Wall -Wextra -Werror clean (CLAUDE.md §2.4).

# CC is make's default, cc: gcc on the Pi and in CI, clang on macOS.

# The tool tests (tests/tools/, D-032) need Python 3.11 or newer, the version Raspberry Pi
# OS ships; the department machines put 3.9 on PATH as python3. Pick the first interpreter
# that is new enough; fall back to python3 so the error, if any, names the version.
PY       ?= $(shell for p in python3 python3.13 python3.12 python3.11; do \
              command -v $$p >/dev/null 2>&1 && \
              $$p -c 'import sys; sys.exit(sys.version_info < (3, 11))' >/dev/null 2>&1 && \
              { echo $$p; exit 0; }; \
            done; echo python3)
CSTD      = -std=c17
WARN      = -Wall -Wextra -Werror -Wshadow -Wconversion -Wvla
OPT      ?= -O2 -g
CPPFLAGS += -Iinclude -D_GNU_SOURCE
CFLAGS   += $(CSTD) $(WARN) $(OPT)
LDLIBS   += -lm -lpthread

BUILD    = build
BIN      = $(BUILD)/bin

ALL_SRC    = $(wildcard src/*/*.c)
# Library objects: everything except the per-daemon entry points, which are main.c and,
# where one directory holds two programs, <name>_main.c.
COMMON_SRC = $(filter-out %/main.c %_main.c,$(ALL_SRC))
COMMON_OBJ = $(COMMON_SRC:%.c=$(BUILD)/%.o)

DAEMONS    = obdd storaged analyzed supervisor obdctl statusd
DAEMON_BIN = $(addprefix $(BIN)/,$(DAEMONS))

TEST_SRC   = $(wildcard tests/test_*.c)
TEST_BIN   = $(TEST_SRC:tests/%.c=$(BIN)/%)

.PHONY: all test asan memcheck soakcheck replay deploy clean boundary boardcheck \
        toolcheck run-status

all: $(DAEMON_BIN)

$(BIN)/obdd:       $(BUILD)/src/obd/main.o        $(COMMON_OBJ)
$(BIN)/storaged:   $(BUILD)/src/store/main.o      $(COMMON_OBJ)
$(BIN)/analyzed:   $(BUILD)/src/analysis/main.o   $(COMMON_OBJ)
$(BIN)/supervisor: $(BUILD)/src/supervisor/main.o $(COMMON_OBJ)
$(BIN)/obdctl:     $(BUILD)/src/interface/main.o  $(COMMON_OBJ)
$(BIN)/statusd:    $(BUILD)/src/interface/statusd_main.o $(COMMON_OBJ)

$(DAEMON_BIN):
	@mkdir -p $(BIN)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDLIBS)

$(BUILD)/%.o: %.c
	@mkdir -p $(dir $@)
	$(CC) $(CPPFLAGS) $(CFLAGS) -MMD -MP -c $< -o $@

$(BIN)/test_%: tests/test_%.c $(COMMON_OBJ)
	@mkdir -p $(BIN)
	$(CC) $(CPPFLAGS) $(CFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDLIBS)

# `all` first: every daemon must compile under the same flags as the tests, so `make asan`
# builds the daemons with the sanitizers too, not only the unit tests.
test: all $(TEST_BIN) boundary boardcheck toolcheck
	@fail=0; for t in $(TEST_BIN); do \
		printf '%-28s ' "$$(basename $$t)"; \
		if $$t; then echo PASS; else echo FAIL; fail=1; fi; done; \
	exit $$fail

# CLAUDE.md §2.1 — a grader must be able to confirm the boundary in sixty seconds (D-038).
# Network code only in src/interface/; Unix sockets only through src/ipc/uds.c. The
# check tests itself first: every case under tests/boundary/cases/bad_* must fail.
boundary:
	@tests/boundary/check.sh --selftest tests/boundary/cases
	@tests/boundary/check.sh . && echo "boundary                     PASS"

# docs/milestones.md is the board (D-020) - every task, question and decision
# in the project is a checkbox there. Validate it in the same gate as the C.
boardcheck:
	@$(PY) tools/test_board.py

# Python tool tests (stdlib unittest, tests/tools/). The venv is made on first use, and
# refreshed when a requirements file changes, so a fresh clone stays green; it needs the
# network for that install. Dev only (D-032).
.venv/.installed: tools/requirements.txt tools/requirements-analysis.txt
	@test -x .venv/bin/python || $(PY) -m venv .venv
	@.venv/bin/pip install -q -r tools/requirements-analysis.txt
	@touch $@

toolcheck: .venv/.installed
	@PYTHONPATH=tools .venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s tests/tools -q && \
		echo "toolcheck                    PASS"

# Sanitized objects live in their own tree. Objects do not depend on the flags that built
# them, so sharing build/ let a plain `make` link against ASan objects and fail, and let
# `make test` rerun sanitized binaries without saying so.
# -fno-sanitize-recover makes a UBSan finding abort the test, so it cannot print PASS.
# LeakSanitizer is on by default on Linux (the Pi, CI); macOS arm64 does not have it.
asan:
	$(MAKE) BUILD=$(BUILD)/asan test \
	  OPT="-O1 -g -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all -fno-omit-frame-pointer"

memcheck: $(TEST_BIN)
	@command -v valgrind >/dev/null 2>&1 || { \
		echo "valgrind not found: run make memcheck on the Pi or Linux (macOS has none)"; exit 1; }
	@for t in $(TEST_BIN); do valgrind --error-exitcode=1 --leak-check=full $$t || exit 1; done

soakcheck: all
	./soak/run_soak.sh --mini

replay: all
	@test -n "$(FIX)" || { echo "usage: make replay FIX=fixtures/<name>"; exit 1; }
	./tools/replay.py --fixture $(FIX) --label replay

# The phone page and API, on synthetic data, until it is wired to the real source (D-045).
# On the Pi, bind the access point's address: make run-status STATUS_ARGS="--bind 192.168.4.1"
STATUS_ARGS ?= --bind 127.0.0.1 --port 8080
run-status: $(BIN)/statusd
	$(BIN)/statusd $(STATUS_ARGS)

deploy: all
	@test -n "$(PI)" || { echo "usage: make deploy PI=pi@<host>"; exit 1; }
	@# Source only: no build trees, no Mac venv, no raw drive data or soak logs, no transcripts.
	rsync -a --exclude /build --exclude /.git --exclude /.venv --exclude /data \
	      --exclude /soak/logs --exclude /partners ./ $(PI):~/carwatch/
	ssh $(PI) 'cd ~/carwatch && make'

clean:
	rm -rf $(BUILD)

-include $(shell find $(BUILD) -name '*.d' 2>/dev/null)

"""obdd end to end at a desk: tools/obdsim.py -> obdd -> ring -> storaged -> the log.

The C daemons as processes, against the fake OBD2 port, with no car. Every sample obdd
pushes must be in the log, labeled synth; the session, supported and static_pids events
must be there too, and a second ECU must be reported once (Camden, 2026-11-08).

import os
import re
import signal
import struct
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time
import unittest
import zlib

import obdsim

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))
# make sets CARWATCH_BIN (build/asan/bin under make asan); run by hand, build/bin.
BIN = os.environ.get("CARWATCH_BIN") or os.path.join(ROOT, "build", "bin")
BIN = BIN if os.path.isabs(BIN) else os.path.join(ROOT, BIN)
RING = "/dev/shm/carwatch-obd"           # RING_NAME_OBD (include/ipc/ring.h)

# include/store/record.h: magic, kind, body_len, seq, mono_ns, wall_ns, src, flags,
# reserved, boot_id; then the body; then a CRC32 of both.
HDR = struct.Struct("<IHHQQQBBHI")  # cspell:disable-line
REC_MAGIC, REC_SAMPLE, REC_EVENT = 0x31525743, 1, 6
SRC_SYNTH = 3

EV_SESSION, EV_STATIC, EV_MULTI, EV_SUPPORTED = 0x0201, 0x0202, 0x020C, 0x020E
RUN_SECONDS = 8


def records(path):
    """(kind, src, body) for every record in a segment, checking each CRC."""
    with open(path, "rb") as f:
        data = f.read()
    off = 0
    while off + HDR.size <= len(data):
        magic, kind, body_len, _seq, _mono, _wall, src, _fl, _res, _boot = \
            HDR.unpack_from(data, off)
        if magic != REC_MAGIC:
            raise AssertionError(f"bad magic at {off}")
        end = off + HDR.size + body_len
        (crc,) = struct.unpack_from("<I", data, end)
        if zlib.crc32(data[off:end]) != crc:
            raise AssertionError(f"bad CRC at {off}")
        yield kind, src, data[off + HDR.size:end]
        off = end + 4

        self.assertIsNotNone(m, "obdd logged its stop line")

        for name in sorted(os.listdir(self.logdir)):
            if name.endswith(".cwr"):
                recs += list(records(os.path.join(self.logdir, name)))
        samples = [(src, body) for kind, src, body in recs if kind == REC_SAMPLE]
        events = {}
        for kind, src, body in recs:
            if kind == REC_EVENT:
                code, n = struct.unpack_from("<HH", body)
                events.setdefault(code, []).append((src, body[4:4 + n].decode("ascii")))

              f"log holds {len(samples)}", file=sys.stderr)
        self.assertEqual(len(samples), pushed, "every pushed sample is in the log once")
        self.assertGreater(rate, 10.0, "obdsim answers about 20 a second")
        self.assertTrue(all(src == SRC_SYNTH for src, _ in samples),
                        "obdsim's banner says SIM: every sample is synth")

        coolant = [struct.unpack_from("<BBB5sf", b) for _, b in samples if b[1] == 0x05]
        self.assertTrue(coolant, "coolant was polled")
        self.assertTrue(all(-40.0 <= c[4] <= 215.0 for c in coolant), "coolant decoded")

        for code, what in ((EV_SESSION, "session"), (EV_SUPPORTED, "supported"),
                           (EV_STATIC, "static_pids"), (EV_MULTI, "multi_ecu")):
            self.assertIn(code, events, f"a {what} event is in the log")
        self.assertTrue(all(src == SRC_SYNTH for evs in events.values() for src, _ in evs),
                        "events keep obdd's label")
        session = events[EV_SESSION][0][1]
        self.assertIn("vin_hash=bb984ebda934", session, "the same hash as obdlib.py")
        self.assertIn("carwatch SIM", session)
        self.assertEqual(events[EV_STATIC][0][1], "none", "obdsim has no static PIDs")
        self.assertIn("n=17", events[EV_SUPPORTED][0][1])
        multi = events[EV_MULTI]
        self.assertEqual(len(multi), 1, "a second ECU is reported once per connection")
        self.assertIn("pid=05 n_ecu=2", multi[0][1])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# A labeled capture through the real pipeline: obdd --replay feeds the ring, storaged
# writes the log (make replay FIX=..., handout §5). Bench mode: obdd makes the ring
# (board benchring), so nothing else may be using it.
#
#   scripts/replay.sh CAPTURE.jsonl [SPEED] [OUT_DIR]
#
# SPEED divides the recorded spacing (1 = real time). OUT_DIR must be new or empty; the
# default is build/replay/<capture>-<time>/. A live capture comes out labeled replay; a
# synth one stays synth (CLAUDE.md §2.7).
set -euo pipefail

CAP=${1:?usage: scripts/replay.sh CAPTURE.jsonl [speed] [out dir]}
SPEED=${2:-1}
BIN=${CARWATCH_BIN:-build/bin}
RING=/dev/shm/carwatch-obd

die() { echo "replay: $*" >&2; exit 1; }

[ -f "$CAP" ] || die "no capture at $CAP"
[ -x "$BIN/obdd" ] && [ -x "$BIN/storaged" ] || die "build first: make"
[ ! -e "$RING" ] || die "$RING exists: is obdd running? stop it first"
case "$(grep -m1 -o '"src":"[a-z]*"' "$CAP" || true)" in
    '"src":"live"' | '"src":"replay"') LABEL=replay ;;
    '"src":"synth"') LABEL=synth ;;
    *) die "$CAP has no live, replay or synth label: refused" ;;
esac
OUT=${3:-build/replay/$(basename "$CAP" .jsonl)-$(date +%Y%m%dT%H%M%S)}
mkdir -p "$OUT"
[ -z "$(ls -A "$OUT")" ] || die "$OUT is not empty"
SOCK=$(mktemp -u "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/carwatch-replay.XXXXXX")

cleanup() {
    [ -n "${OBDD:-}" ] && kill "$OBDD" 2>/dev/null || true
    [ -n "${STORE:-}" ] && kill "$STORE" 2>/dev/null || true
    rm -f "$RING" "$SOCK"
}
trap cleanup EXIT

"$BIN/obdd" --replay "$CAP" --speed "$SPEED" --create-ring --events "$SOCK" \
    >"$OUT/obdd.log" 2>&1 &
OBDD=$!
for _ in $(seq 100); do [ -e "$RING" ] && break; sleep 0.05; done
[ -e "$RING" ] || die "obdd did not make the ring: see $OUT/obdd.log"
"$BIN/storaged" --dir "$OUT" --src "$LABEL" --events "$SOCK" >"$OUT/storaged.log" 2>&1 &
STORE=$!

OBDD_RC=0
wait "$OBDD" || OBDD_RC=$?
OBDD=
sleep 1.5                       # one batch (D-035): storaged drains what is left
kill -TERM "$STORE"
STORE_RC=0
wait "$STORE" || STORE_RC=$?
STORE=

grep -h -E "replay_done|replay_refused|stop samples" "$OUT/obdd.log" "$OUT/storaged.log" |
    sed 's/^.* pid=[0-9]* //'
echo "replay: label=$LABEL obdd=$OBDD_RC storaged=$STORE_RC log in $OUT"
[ "$OBDD_RC" -eq 0 ] && [ "$STORE_RC" -eq 0 ]

# carwatch — CS370 term project
# Systems core is C17 and must stay -Wall -Wextra -Werror clean (CLAUDE.md §2.4).

# CC is make's default, cc: gcc on the Pi and in CI, clang on macOS.

# The tool tests (tests/tools/, D-032) need Python 3.11 or newer, the version Raspberry Pi
# OS ships; the department machines put 3.9 on PATH as python3. Pick the first interpreter
# that is new enough; fall back to python3 so the error, if any, names the version.
PY       ?= $(shell for p in python3 python3.13 python3.12 python3.11; do \
              command -v $$p >/dev/null 2>&1 && \
              $$p -c 'import sys; sys.exit(sys.version_info < (3, 11))' >/dev/null 2>&1 && \
              { echo $$p; exit 0; }; \
            done; echo python3)
CSTD      = -std=c17
WARN      = -Wall -Wextra -Werror -Wshadow -Wconversion -Wvla
OPT      ?= -O2 -g
CPPFLAGS += -Iinclude -D_GNU_SOURCE
CFLAGS   += $(CSTD) $(WARN) $(OPT)
LDLIBS   += -lm -lpthread

BUILD    = build
BIN      = $(BUILD)/bin

ALL_SRC    = $(wildcard src/*/*.c)
# Library objects: everything except the per-daemon entry points, which are main.c and,
# where one directory holds two programs, <name>_main.c.
COMMON_SRC = $(filter-out %/main.c %_main.c,$(ALL_SRC))
COMMON_OBJ = $(COMMON_SRC:%.c=$(BUILD)/%.o)

DAEMONS    = obdd storaged analyzed supervisor obdctl statusd
DAEMON_BIN = $(addprefix $(BIN)/,$(DAEMONS))

TEST_SRC   = $(wildcard tests/test_*.c)
TEST_BIN   = $(TEST_SRC:tests/%.c=$(BIN)/%)

.PHONY: all test asan memcheck soakcheck replay deploy clean boundary boardcheck \
        toolcheck run-status

all: $(DAEMON_BIN)

$(BIN)/obdd:       $(BUILD)/src/obd/main.o        $(COMMON_OBJ)
$(BIN)/storaged:   $(BUILD)/src/store/main.o      $(COMMON_OBJ)
$(BIN)/analyzed:   $(BUILD)/src/analysis/main.o   $(COMMON_OBJ)
$(BIN)/supervisor: $(BUILD)/src/supervisor/main.o $(COMMON_OBJ)
$(BIN)/obdctl:     $(BUILD)/src/interface/main.o  $(COMMON_OBJ)
$(BIN)/statusd:    $(BUILD)/src/interface/statusd_main.o $(COMMON_OBJ)

$(DAEMON_BIN):
	@mkdir -p $(BIN)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDLIBS)

$(BUILD)/%.o: %.c
	@mkdir -p $(dir $@)
	$(CC) $(CPPFLAGS) $(CFLAGS) -MMD -MP -c $< -o $@

$(BIN)/test_%: tests/test_%.c $(COMMON_OBJ)
	@mkdir -p $(BIN)
	$(CC) $(CPPFLAGS) $(CFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDLIBS)

# `all` first: every daemon must compile under the same flags as the tests, so `make asan`
# builds the daemons with the sanitizers too, not only the unit tests.
test: all $(TEST_BIN) boundary boardcheck toolcheck
	@fail=0; for t in $(TEST_BIN); do \
		printf '%-28s ' "$$(basename $$t)"; \
		if $$t; then echo PASS; else echo FAIL; fail=1; fi; done; \
	exit $$fail

# CLAUDE.md §2.1 — a grader must be able to confirm the boundary in sixty seconds (D-038).
# Network code only in src/interface/; Unix sockets only through src/ipc/uds.c. The
# check tests itself first: every case under tests/boundary/cases/bad_* must fail.
boundary:
	@tests/boundary/check.sh --selftest tests/boundary/cases
	@tests/boundary/check.sh . && echo "boundary                     PASS"

# docs/milestones.md is the board (D-020) - every task, question and decision
# in the project is a checkbox there. Validate it in the same gate as the C.
boardcheck:
	@$(PY) tools/test_board.py

# Python tool tests (stdlib unittest, tests/tools/). The venv is made on first use, and
# refreshed when a requirements file changes, so a fresh clone stays green; it needs the
# network for that install. Dev only (D-032).
.venv/.installed: tools/requirements.txt tools/requirements-analysis.txt
	@test -x .venv/bin/python || $(PY) -m venv .venv
	@.venv/bin/pip install -q -r tools/requirements-analysis.txt
	@touch $@

# CARWATCH_BIN: where this build put the daemons, so the end-to-end tool tests run the
# sanitized ones under make asan.
toolcheck: .venv/.installed
	@PYTHONPATH=tools CARWATCH_BIN=$(BIN) .venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s tests/tools -q && \
		echo "toolcheck                    PASS"

# Sanitized objects live in their own tree. Objects do not depend on the flags that built
# them, so sharing build/ let a plain `make` link against ASan objects and fail, and let
# `make test` rerun sanitized binaries without saying so.
# -fno-sanitize-recover makes a UBSan finding abort the test, so it cannot print PASS.
# LeakSanitizer is on by default on Linux (the Pi, CI); macOS arm64 does not have it.

	@command -v valgrind >/dev/null 2>&1 || { \
		echo "valgrind not found: run make memcheck on the Pi or Linux (macOS has none)"; exit 1; }

# On the Pi, bind the access point's address: make run-status STATUS_ARGS="--bind 192.168.4.1"

	@# Source only: no build trees, no Mac venv, no raw drive data or soak logs, no transcripts.
	rsync -a --exclude /build --exclude /.git --exclude /.venv --exclude /data \
	      --exclude /soak/logs --exclude /partners ./ $(PI):~/carwatch/
	ssh $(PI) 'cd ~/carwatch && make'

clean:
	rm -rf $(BUILD)

-include $(shell find $(BUILD) -name '*.d' 2>/dev/null)

"""obdd --replay through storaged (scripts/replay.sh, make replay): a capture's samples
reach the log once each, with the label the rule gives them, the value obdlog decoded,
and the capture's timing divided by the speed (Camden, 2026-11-08: the replay is C).

Runs where make has built the daemons; skips elsewhere. Uses the real ring name, so it
must not run on a box whose obdd is live.
"""
import json
import os
import struct
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time
import unittest

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from test_obdd_e2e import BIN, REC_EVENT, REC_SAMPLE, ROOT, records  # noqa: E402

SYNTH = os.path.join(ROOT, "fixtures", "synth", "drive-cycle-synth.jsonl")
FORESTER = os.path.join(ROOT, "captures", "forester", "20261028T220659.957", "drive.jsonl")
SRC_REPLAY, SRC_SYNTH = 2, 3
EV_SESSION, EV_REPLAY = 0x0201, 0x020D


def capture(path):
    """(samples, first t_mono, last t_mono) of an obdlog capture."""
    with open(path) as f:
        rows = [json.loads(line) for line in f]
    samples = [r for r in rows if r.get("type") == "sample"]
    return samples, samples[0]["t_mono"], samples[-1]["t_mono"]


def f32(x):
    return struct.unpack("<f", struct.pack("<f", x))[0]


@unittest.skipUnless(sys.platform.startswith("linux"), "the ring is POSIX shm on Linux")
@unittest.skipUnless(os.path.exists(os.path.join(BIN, "obdd")) and
                     os.path.exists(os.path.join(BIN, "storaged")),
                     f"{BIN}/obdd and storaged not built: run make first")
class Replay(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.dir = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()

    def tearDown(self):
        self.dir.cleanup()

    def replay(self, path, speed, out="log"):
        out = os.path.join(self.dir.name, out)
        env = dict(os.environ, CARWATCH_BIN=BIN)
        t = time.monotonic()
        r = subprocess.run([os.path.join(ROOT, "scripts", "replay.sh"), path, str(speed), out],
                           cwd=ROOT, env=env, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=120)
        elapsed = time.monotonic() - t
        recs = []
        if os.path.isdir(out):
            for name in sorted(os.listdir(out)):
                if name.endswith(".cwr"):
                    recs += list(records(os.path.join(out, name)))
        return r, recs, elapsed

    def check(self, path, speed, label):
        want, t0, t1 = capture(path)
        r, recs, elapsed = self.replay(path, speed)
        self.assertEqual(r.returncode, 0, r.stdout + r.stderr)
        samples = [(src, body) for kind, src, body in recs if kind == REC_SAMPLE]
        self.assertEqual(len(samples), len(want), "every sample of the capture, once")
        self.assertTrue(all(src == label for src, _ in samples), "the label the rule gives")

        # In order, with obdlog's value for every PID it decoded (NaN where it wrote null).
        for (_, body), row in zip(samples, want):
            _mode, pid, _n, _raw, value = struct.unpack("<BBB5sf", body)
            self.assertEqual(pid, int(row["pid"], 16))
            if row["val"] is None:
                self.assertNotEqual(value, value, f"PID {row['pid']} has no formula: NaN")
            else:
                self.assertEqual(value, f32(row["val"]), f"PID {row['pid']} {row['raw']}")

        codes = [struct.unpack_from("<H", b)[0] for k, _, b in recs if k == REC_EVENT]
        self.assertIn(EV_REPLAY, codes, "the replay says what it replayed")
        self.assertIn(EV_SESSION, codes, "and the recorded session")
        self.assertGreater(elapsed, (t1 - t0) / speed * 0.9, "the recorded spacing is kept")
        return elapsed

    def test_a_live_capture_comes_out_replay_with_obdlogs_values(self):
        e = self.check(FORESTER, 50, SRC_REPLAY)
        print(f"\n  forester: 1113 samples, 53.8 s of drive at 50x in {e:.1f} s",
              file=sys.stderr)

    def test_a_synth_capture_stays_synth(self):
        self.check(SYNTH, 50, SRC_SYNTH)

    def test_an_unlabeled_capture_is_refused(self):
        bad = os.path.join(self.dir.name, "bad.jsonl")
        with open(bad, "w") as f:
            f.write('{"type":"header","seq":0}\n{"type":"sample","pid":"0C","raw":"0A 10",'
                    '"t_mono":1.0}\n')
        r, recs, _ = self.replay(bad, 1)
        self.assertNotEqual(r.returncode, 0)
        self.assertIn("refused", r.stderr)
        self.assertEqual([k for k, _, _ in recs if k == REC_SAMPLE], [])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# A labeled capture through the real pipeline: obdd --replay feeds the ring, storaged
# writes the log (make replay FIX=..., handout §5). Bench mode: obdd makes the ring
# (board benchring), so nothing else may be using it.
#
#   scripts/replay.sh CAPTURE.jsonl [SPEED] [OUT_DIR]
#
# SPEED divides the recorded spacing (1 = real time). OUT_DIR must be new or empty; the
# default is build/replay/<capture>-<time>/. A live capture comes out labeled replay; a
# synth one stays synth (CLAUDE.md §2.7).
set -euo pipefail

CAP=${1:?usage: scripts/replay.sh CAPTURE.jsonl [speed] [out dir]}
SPEED=${2:-1}
BIN=${CARWATCH_BIN:-build/bin}
RING=/dev/shm/carwatch-obd

die() { echo "replay: $*" >&2; exit 1; }

[ -f "$CAP" ] || die "no capture at $CAP"
[ -x "$BIN/obdd" ] && [ -x "$BIN/storaged" ] || die "build first: make"
[ ! -e "$RING" ] || die "$RING exists: is obdd running? stop it first"
case "$(grep -m1 -o '"src":"[a-z]*"' "$CAP" || true)" in
    '"src":"live"' | '"src":"replay"') LABEL=replay ;;
    '"src":"synth"') LABEL=synth ;;
    *) die "$CAP has no live, replay or synth label: refused" ;;
esac
OUT=${3:-build/replay/$(basename "$CAP" .jsonl)-$(date +%Y%m%dT%H%M%S)}
mkdir -p "$OUT"
[ -z "$(ls -A "$OUT")" ] || die "$OUT is not empty"
SOCK=$(mktemp -u "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/carwatch-replay.XXXXXX")

cleanup() {
    if [ -n "${OBDD:-}" ]; then kill "$OBDD" 2>/dev/null || true; fi
    if [ -n "${STORE:-}" ]; then kill "$STORE" 2>/dev/null || true; fi
    rm -f "$RING" "$SOCK"
}
trap cleanup EXIT

"$BIN/obdd" --replay "$CAP" --speed "$SPEED" --create-ring --events "$SOCK" \
    >"$OUT/obdd.log" 2>&1 &
OBDD=$!
for _ in $(seq 100); do [ -e "$RING" ] && break; sleep 0.05; done
[ -e "$RING" ] || die "obdd did not make the ring: see $OUT/obdd.log"
"$BIN/storaged" --dir "$OUT" --src "$LABEL" --events "$SOCK" >"$OUT/storaged.log" 2>&1 &
STORE=$!

OBDD_RC=0
wait "$OBDD" || OBDD_RC=$?
OBDD=
sleep 1.5                       # one batch (D-035): storaged drains what is left
kill -TERM "$STORE"
STORE_RC=0
wait "$STORE" || STORE_RC=$?
STORE=

grep -h -E "replay_done|replay_refused|stop samples" "$OUT/obdd.log" "$OUT/storaged.log" |
    sed 's/^.* pid=[0-9]* //'
echo "replay: label=$LABEL obdd=$OBDD_RC storaged=$STORE_RC log in $OUT"
[ "$OBDD_RC" -eq 0 ] && [ "$STORE_RC" -eq 0 ]
